item.title: Rams fans criticize controversial penalty after upset loss raises questions about officiating
item.description: Mactrunk/Depositphotos 358150090 Ringo Chiu/Shutterstock.com How a late penalty shaped the Rams’ loss to Arizona The Los Angeles Rams suffered an 18–16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals after a disputed late penalty helped set up a game-winning field goal as time expired. Cornerback Josh Wallace was flagged for unnecessary roughness following a 21-yard completion, sparking criticism from fans and questions from FOX Sports rules analyst Mike Pereira. The defeat left both teams with 2–4 records after six games, adding pressure to the Rams’ season. vverve/Depositphotos Josh Wallace draws a late penalty Rams cornerback Josh Wallace was penalized for unnecessary roughness after Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett completed a 21-yard pass to receiver Jalen Brooks late in the fourth quarter. Officials assessed a 15-yard penalty against Los Angeles, adding to Arizona’s gain and moving the Cardinals into favorable field position. The decision became the central officiating controversy following the game. bellafotosolo/Depositphotos The call puts Arizona in scoring range The penalty followed a 21-yard completion that brought Arizona closer to field-goal range with less than a minute remaining. The additional 15 yards helped the Cardinals advance into Rams territory after Los Angeles had taken a late lead. Kicker Chad Ryland subsequently made the game-winning field goal as time expired, completing Arizona’s comeback. Mactrunk/Depositphotos Rams fans question the officials’ decision Following the game, Rams supporters and other football fans criticized the unnecessary roughness call on social media. Several posts questioned whether Wallace’s contact with Brooks justified a 15-yard penalty at such a late stage. The online reaction reflected disagreement over the ruling, although social media responses alone cannot establish whether officials applied the NFL’s rules incorrectly. zhukovsky/Depositphotos Mike Pereira weighs in on the ruling FOX Sports rules analyst Mike Pereira discussed whether the penalty against Wallace should have stood. Pereira noted that replay review could potentially address the call if there was no contact, while also acknowledging that contact occurred. His analysis focused on whether the contact met the standard for a foul, highlighting the distinction between visible contact and a punishable violation. katatonia82/Depositphotos Replay footage fuels debate over contact Replays of Wallace’s contact with Brooks became a major part of the discussion after the game. Some observers argued that the footage did not support the severity of the penalty, while others noted that Wallace moved into the receiver during the play. The disagreement centered on the nature of the contact and whether it warranted the officials’ decision. The defeat left both teams with 2–4 records after six games, adding pressure to the Rams’ season. vverve/Depositphotos Josh Wallace draws a late penalty Rams cornerback Josh Wallace was penalized for unnecessary roughness after Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett completed a 21-yard pass to receiver Jalen Brooks late in the fourth quarter. Officials assessed a 15-yard penalty against Los Angeles, adding to Arizona’s gain and moving the Cardinals into favorable field position. The decision became the central officiating controversy following the game. bellafotosolo/Depositphotos The call puts Arizona in scoring range The penalty followed a 21-yard completion that brought Arizona closer to field-goal range with less than a minute remaining. The additional 15 yards helped the Cardinals advance into Rams territory after Los Angeles had taken a late lead. Kicker Chad Ryland subsequently made the game-winning field goal as time expired, completing Arizona’s comeback. Mactrunk/Depositphotos Rams fans question the officials’ decision Following the game, Rams supporters and other football fans criticized the unnecessary roughness call on social media. Several posts questioned whether Wallace’s contact with Brooks justified a 15-yard penalty at such a late stage. The online reaction reflected disagreement over the ruling, although social media responses alone cannot establish whether officials applied the NFL’s rules incorrectly. zhukovsky/Depositphotos Mike Pereira weighs in on the ruling FOX Sports rules analyst Mike Pereira discussed whether the penalty against Wallace should have stood. Pereira noted that replay review could potentially address the call if there was no contact, while also acknowledging that contact occurred. His analysis focused on whether the contact met the standard for a foul, highlighting the distinction between visible contact and a punishable violation. katatonia82/Depositphotos Replay footage fuels debate over contact Replays of Wallace’s contact with Brooks became a major part of the discussion after the game. Some observers argued that the footage did not support the severity of the penalty, while others noted that Wallace moved into the receiver during the play. The disagreement centered on the nature of the contact and whether it warranted the officials’ decision. Interesting fact : The Los Angeles Rams were the first NFL team to move to the West Coast. noonie/Depositphotos Arizona capitalizes on the final opportunity The Cardinals took advantage of their improved field position to set up a late scoring attempt. Ryland converted the decisive kick as the clock expired, giving Arizona an 18–16 win. He finished the contest with six field goals, including the game-winner, while quarterback Brissett helped lead the closing drive that put the Cardinals within range. Interesting fact : The NFL introduced instant replay in 1986 . The system allows officials to review certain plays, and the league continues to update its replay procedures to improve accuracy and consistency. Ringo Chiu/Shutterstock.com Matthew Stafford leads a late scoring drive Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford completed 25 of 33 passes for 222 yards and 2 touchdowns against Arizona. His 6-yard touchdown pass to tight end Colby Parkinson put Los Angeles ahead 16–15 with 47 seconds remaining. The Rams converted the extra point to take the lead, but their defense could not prevent Arizona from answering with a game-winning field goal as time expired. Depositphotos A kicker injury complicates the Rams’ game Los Angeles lost newly signed kicker Blake Grupe to a knee injury during the first quarter after he tackled Cardinals returner Devin Duvernay on the kickoff following a successful 44-yard field goal. Grupe did not return to the game. Rams punter Ethan Evans subsequently converted the extra point after Colby Parkinson’s late touchdown, helping Los Angeles take a 16–15 lead with 47 seconds remaining. kovop/Shutterstock.com The defeat follows another disputed call The latest controversy came weeks after a disputed defensive pass interference penalty against Wallace in the Rams’ September 27 loss to the Denver Broncos. That earlier ruling erased an interception and helped Denver continue its game-winning drive in a 30–26 victory. Rams coach Sean McVay later said the NFL acknowledged that the pass interference call was incorrect, providing context for the renewed debate over officiating. Depositphotos Sean McVay faces questions about the loss Rams head coach Sean McVay has emphasized that his team must improve rather than rely on officiating explanations after close defeats. Following the earlier loss to Denver, he said the team needed to learn from the experience and focus on execution. The Cardinals defeat added another difficult result to Los Angeles’ season, with the late penalty becoming a prominent talking point. galecophoto/Depositphotos The Rams’ record falls to 2–4 The loss left both the Rams and Cardinals with 2–4 records through six games of the 2026 regular season. Los Angeles entered the matchup seeking a win but surrendered its late advantage in the final minute. The result added pressure to the Rams’ campaign, while Arizona gained a valuable divisional victory through Ryland’s final kick. The Bills and Rams delivered a memorable matchup, and the exchange between their quarterbacks added another talking point for fans. Discover Matthew Stafford’s pre-overtime joke to Josh Allen emerging in mic’d-up footage . watman/Depositphotos Officiating consistency remains under scrutiny The Rams’ latest defeat has renewed discussion about how officials judge contact involving receivers and defensive backs. The penalty against Wallace directly affected Arizona’s final drive, but Los Angeles also had opportunities to secure the win before that sequence. Evaluating the decision requires examining the applicable NFL rules, available replay footage and any subsequent league explanation rather than relying solely on fan reactions. Travis Kelce’s popularity extends beyond his career with the Kansas City Chiefs, opening doors to opportunities in entertainment and business. Explore Travis Kelce drawing interest from three possible bidders outside football . Share your opinion on the controversial penalty in the comments, and like this post if you think officiating decisions deserve closer scrutiny in crucial moments. Do you agree with the call, or should the officials have let the play stand? This slideshow was made with AI assistance and human editing. item.title: Barcelona sensation matches Mbappe’s Champions League record after scoring against PSG
item.description: Barcelona sensation matches Mbappe’s Champions League record after scoring against PSG Lamine Yamal continued his remarkable start to the season despite Barcelona’s 2-4 Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain, scoring at the Parc des Princes to reach 20 goal contributions across all competitions. With El Clasico against Real Madrid approaching , the Barcelona winger is combining prolific output with creative influence at a rate rarely seen at his age. Notably, the 19-year-old’s latest goal also brought him level with Kylian Mbappe’s record of 13 Champions League goals before turning 20, showing his growing impact on European football’s biggest stage. Yamal reaches 20 goal contributions for Barcelona Yamal’s goal against PSG was another example of his technical quality, with the winger finding the net through an exquisite toe-poke finish. It took his season tally to 10 goals, while his 10 assists brought his total involvement to 20 of Barcelona’s 50 goals. That means Yamal has contributed directly to 40% of the team’s goals this season. Lamine Yamal has now scored 13 goals in the UEFA Champions League. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) To put it in perspective, there is no precedent for a Barcelona player reaching a 10-goal, 10-assist split this early in a season, not even Lionel Messi, who recorded 25 goal contributions in the 2011-12 campaign, with 16 goals and nine assists. Barcelona number 10 draws level with Mbappe Yamal’s European numbers provide another measure of his progress. After scoring against PSG, he has registered 13 goals and 13 assists in 36 Champions League appearances, matching Mbappe’s record of 13 goals in the competition before his 20th birthday. The comparison places Yamal alongside one of the most productive forwards of his generation at the same stage of their careers. However, their records reflect different attacking profiles, with Yamal’s assist tally highlighting the creative dimension of his game alongside his finishing. At his current rate, the Barcelona teenager has a strong opportunity to move beyond Mbappe’s benchmark before turning 20. Yamal gives Barcelona a major weapon before El Clasico Lamine Yamal is one goal away from breaking Kylian Mbappe’s record. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) Indeed, Barcelona will be disappointed by the result in Paris, but Yamal’s performance offered an important positive ahead of the meeting with Real Madrid. His ability to create and score makes him one of Flick’s most influential attacking players, particularly when opponents concentrate their defensive efforts on limiting his space. The challenge now is to test that brilliance against the strongest opposition. PSG exposed Barcelona’s defensive weaknesses, but Yamal demonstrated that the team still possesses the attacking quality to trouble elite sides. With El Clasico approaching, Real Madrid will have to account for a winger who is producing goals and assists at an exceptional rate.

item.title: Borussia Dortmund’s Gregor Kobel praises ‘machine’ Serhou Guirassy
item.description: Borussia Dortmund’s Gregor Kobel praises ‘machine’ Serhou Guirassy Serhou Guirassy’s brace against Azerbaijan side Sabah FK secured Borussia Dortmund a 2-1 victory, ending a run of three defeats across all competitions. Speaking to DAZN post-match, BVB custodian Gregor Kobel praised his Guinean teammate. “Serhou is a machine, and I don’t really have to say much more,” he expressed. Guirassy, though, challenged his teammates , and himself, to maintain high standards. “We’re top players, so we have to work on that – myself included,” the forward explained.” The 30-year-old’s brace brought an end to Dortmund’s winless run having played out 2-2 and 0-0 draws against Werder Bremen and Union Berlin in the Bundesliga, either side of a 1-0 loss against Bodø/Glimt. After successive Bundesliga draws, Dortmund will hope to secure a return to winning ways when they host Eintracht Frankfurt on 24 October before welcoming Bremen back to the Westfalenstadion three days later in the DFB Pokal, before Matchday 8’s Klassiker against Bayern Munich. GGFN | Daniel Pinder

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s troublesome 1000 goals journey continues
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo’s troublesome 1000 goals journey continues appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Playing his first game for Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia after the Portugal fiasco, Cristiano Ronaldo ’s woeful run seems to continue. Ronaldo missed a penalty in his first match since his Portugal suspension, as Al-Nassr managed to beat Saudi Pro League rivals Neom 1-0. Ronaldo received a chance to give this team the advantage but missed the chance when he fired his spot-kick wide in first-half stoppage time after Neom defender Mohammed Al Dossary had brought down João Félix in the box. However, Ronaldo missed the penalty kick by miles. Once regarded as one of the penalty takers of the modern era, it now seems Ronaldo’s age is catching up to him . Joao Félix, Ronaldo’s Portugal and Al-Nassr teammate, struck the winner just after the hour mark when he fired home from the edge of the area. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Earlier, Ronaldo was suspended for 30 days and fined €255 ($285.90) after walking out on his national team earlier this month during the UEFA Nations League, following a misunderstanding with his team and manager. If the suspension dates back to the time of the provisional decision, he will be able to participate in his country’s next game versus Denmark on Nov. 14, 2026. Struggling to reach the legendary 1000-goal landmark, Ronaldo recently also found himself the subject of former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag’s frustrating comments . “He let the team down, and he let me down too, because we were planning for the season with him in it,” Ten Hag said. However, despite the controversial statements, Ronaldo has not yet officially commented on them. Related: Cristiano Ronaldo blasted by former Manchester United boss : ‘He let the team down’

item.title: College Football Big Ten power rankings entering Week 8
item.description: Saturday of Week 7 in college football may have been the epitome of Big Ten football. On Saturday, only two Big Ten teams scored 25 or more points: Rutgers and Maryland, who went head-to-head against the other’s terrible defense in a 37-30 slopfest. Saturday brought a lot of close games and lower-scoring contests than anticipated. That’s Big Ten football in a nutshell. MORE: 4 biggest risers in College Football after Week 7 Ranks 10-6 Oct 16, 2026; West Lafayette, Indiana, USA; Purdue Boilermakers quarterback Ryan Browne (15) motions to his team during the second half against the Washington Huskies at Ross-Ade Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Marc Lebryk-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) 10. Purdue Maybe Purdue isn’t there just yet. At home, on national TV, on Friday night, the Boilermakers were not at their best in a 38-26 loss to Washington. Ryan Browne was inefficient through the air, and Fame Ijeboi was bottled up all night long. They’re better than the Purdue of old, but the rebuild is not finished. 9. Washington Should Washington have let Demond Williams Jr. walk in the offseason? After a rocky start to the season and numerous injuries, the Huskies offense finally got going in a 38-26 win over Purdue… with Stanford transfer Elijah Brown at QB. We now have a QB controversy on our hands. 8. Northwestern Good thing style points don’t matter. It wasn’t pretty, but the Wildcats came from behind to defeat Michigan State 24-21. It would have been an incredibly embarrassing loss for Northwestern, as new Michigan State coach Pat Fitzgerald was formerly Northwestern’s coach before a controversial exit. 7. Wisconsin In what may have been the ugliest game of the weekend, the Badgers came up short in a 17-7 loss to UCLA. The defense kept getting stops, but the offense just couldn’t get more points on the scoreboard. Colton Joseph is electric as a runner, but needs better mechanics and better weapons for this offense to be a serious passing threat. 6. Iowa There were 0 points scored on the Iowa defense in Week 7. Well, it was their Bye week, but still! In Week 8, the Hawkeyes travel to Minnesota for an old Big Ten West rivalry. I would expect Jeremy Hecklinski to start for Iowa after his great performance against Washington. item.title: LFP launches Ligue 1 TV rights tender amid ‘new context’
item.description: LFP launches Ligue 1 TV rights tender amid ‘new context’ The LFP (Ligue de Football Professionnel) have launched an auction for the rights to broadcast from the start of next season, running through until 2032, it was confirmed by Vincent Labrune on Wednesday. Ligue 1 is currently broadcast by an in-house broadcaster, Ligue 1 Plus, and is currently into its second season of broadcasting the league. Whilst, from an editorial perspective, it has been a success, that is not the case from a financial perspective. Most clubs have sought to move away from the league-owned broadcaster due to the lack of income it has provided. Income from TV rights has been in freefall ever since the MediaPro withdrawal. Prior to the creation of Ligue 1 Plus, DAZN and BeIN Sports had held the rights, with the latter broadcasting just one game. The former pulled out of the deal to broadcast France’s top flight after just one season. Announcing that there will be a new round of bidding for a new five-year cycle from 2027 until 2032, Labrune spoke of a “new context” that is more favourable. He added, “For several months, there have been a certain number of registered concrete interests from different actors.” Due to a very recent change in legislation, the rights can now be sold in a single bundle, thus offering exclusivity rights. The bidding will run from 3rd November until 7th December, the LFP have announced. GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: Dolphins news: Week 7 roster moves include addition of Zane Gonzalez, cut Storm Duck
item.description: HOUSTON, TX - DECEMBER 15: Storm Duck #36 of the Miami Dolphins lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on December 15, 2024 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Tuesday was a busy day for the Miami Dolphins, with the front office making several roster moves. The Dolphins swapped kickers on Tuesday, bring back Zane Gonzalez and waiving Riley Patterson. Patterson was 7-for-0 on field goals this season and 5-for-6 on extra point attempts. After connecting on 93.1 percent of this field goal attempts, including 3-of-4 from over 50 yards, last year, Patterson’s accuracy seem to fall off this year, but a bigger issue seemed to be on kickoffs. “We did try to kick them out of the end zone; that was discussed and just not executed the way that we wanted it to be…yeah, several of them were supposed to be touchbacks and weren’t,” head coach Jeff Hafley explained on Monday when asked about the team’s special teams issues and lack of simply kicking the ball for touchbacks rather than relying on the coverage unit. The Dolphins held a tryout for kickers on Tuesday, including former seven-time Pro Bowl selection Justin Tucker, and ultimately brought back Gonzalez. The Cleveland Browns’ 2017 seventh-round draft pick, Gonzalez landed on injured reserve during the preseason with Miami this past summer. He was released with an injury settlement and now returns to to the Dolphins, signing with the practice squad. Miami was not done with their roster moves. They also promoted rookie edge rusher Rodney McGraw from the practice squad and waived edge rusher Andre Jones Jr. The potentially surprise move of the day came with the news the Dolphins were waiving cornerback Storm Duck. A 2024 undrafted free agent out of Louisville, Duck was on the physically unable to perform list this year as he recovered from a knee injury sustained last year. He returned to practice three weeks ago, and the team has until today to decide whether to add him to the active 53-man roster or keep him on the PUP for the rest of the year. item.title: Vols Were Easier Than Expected. Kansas? Won’t Be That Simple.
item.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 20: Patrick Ngongba II #21 of the Duke Blue Devils reacts following a basket during the first half of the game against the Tennessee Volunteers at Cameron Indoor Stadium on October 20, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images I n an interesting way, Duke’s preseason has moved from easy (Belmont), to theoretically more challenging (Tennessee), to suddenly much more difficult this Sunday (at Kansas). Kansas would already be a real challenge with familiar faces like Tre White, Kohl Rosario, Dennis Parker, and Melvin Council. That should be more difficult by far than either Belmont or Tennessee proved to be. And also, if you didn’t know, the Jayhawks picked up former Blue Devil Christian Reeves, who did well last season at College of Charleston. And just this week, Kansas added Trey Kaufman-Renn, who had an outstanding career at Purdue. Kansas also has a pretty good shot at matching Duke’s size, with the 7-2 Reeves, 7-0 Grant Mordini, 7-0 Paul Mbiya, 6-10 Davion Adkins, and the 6-9 Kaufman-Renn. And of course, they have perhaps the best freshman in the nation in 6-8 Tyran Stokes. We’ll do a full preview closer to Sunday, but for now, we just wanted to touch on this game a bit, because it should be a good bit tougher than Tennessee was, whether or not Kaufman-Renn plays (like a lot of players this year, his eligibility is in the hands of a judge), and a good bit more interesting as well. item.title: PSG winger Kvaratskhelia's season in doubt after torn ACL
item.description: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffered an ACL injury during Paris Saint-Germain's win against Barcelona (JULIEN DE ROSA) Paris Saint-Germain could be without star winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for the rest of the season after he tore his ACL in the Champions League win against Barcelona while Ousmane Dembele also faces weeks out of action, the European champions said on Wednesday. PSG said Kvaratskhelia "is set to undergo surgery in the coming days" after he suffered the injury in the 4-2 league phase win against Barcelona at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday. Kvaratskhelia slumped to the turf without any apparent contact and left the pitch just before the hour mark. The club gave no timeline for his return to action but recovery from anterior cruciate ligament surgery typically takes between six and nine months, meaning the 25-year-old Georgia international can at best hope to be back for the closing stages of the season. Former Napoli winger Kvaratskhelia has established himself as one of Europe's most exciting attacking players and played a leading role in helping PSG to win back-to-back Champions League titles in the last two seasons. Like Dembele, he is one of the contenders for the Ballon d'Or, which will be awarded on Monday. The club said Dembele, the current Ballon d'Or holder, as well as PSG's captain and central defender Marquinhos will both be sidelined for "several weeks" with thigh injuries they suffered in the win against Barcelona. Dembele, 29, had to be substituted after 20 minutes due to his injury while Brazil international Marquinhos was withdrawn after an hour. France international Dembele, who scored six goals at this year's World Cup, struggled with injuries last season and PSG coach Luis Enrique used him sparingly in Ligue 1, preferring to keep him for Champions League games. Dembele was also beset by injuries at his previous club, Barcelona. In the absence of two of their attacking stars, PSG will need to rely on summer signings Maghnes Akliouche, Mika Godts and Ferran Torres, the Spain international who scored the winning goal in the World Cup final in July. PSG host Ligue 1 leaders Lyon on Sunday in their next domestic match and they are next in action in the Champions League on November 3, with a trip to Spanish side Villarreal. ali-rbo/gj

item.title: Q&A: Joe Burrow on his passion for chess and designing his own set
item.description: Joe Burrow is a truly gifted quarterback. He has a National Championship, title game Offensive MVP and Heisman Trophy to his name from his time at LSU, and he was drafted No. 1 overall by the Cincinnati Bengals in 2020. Burrow helped the Bengals make the Super Bowl in 2021, and he's been part of their potent offense. But the talented footballer is also a savvy chess player. Through a partnership with Chrome, Burrow got a chance to dip into his creative side and his love for chess to design his own set. For The Win had a chance to interview Burrow about his hobby, its impact on his football game and why he wanted to participate in this collaboration. This interview has been edited for length and clarity. You've been described as a lifelong chess player. How young were you when you started, and what has your journey been like with chess? I don't remember exactly how old I was, but it was in elementary school for sure. Indoor recess when it was raining outside, I would start playing. I didn't play too much when I was younger. I don't remember exactly when Chess.com became a thing, but I wasn't playing online like that when I was younger. During COVID, I started really getting into openings and lines and actually how to play. Who taught you how to play? A friend taught me to play, and then we just we would just play. I don't remember playing with my family ever. Really, I don't think they even know how to play. Do you still play online? Do people know it's you? I do, and they do. They didn't for a while, and then when we went to the Super Bowl in 2021, my my username got leaked. I play a lot during the season because you have like a 10 minute break in between meetings, and I can sit there, or I can play a game of chess. My hours got leaked, and that was that wasn't good for me at the time. Is it a relaxation thing? Do you think it's a keep your mind sharp thing? A combination? How do you approach your chess time now? Yeah, it's a combination of everything. During the season, I don't really have social media too much, and I'm not a huge reader. I'll read articles and and papers and whatnot, but I'm not super into books that much. So, just playing a lot of chess. It's kind of all the above -- keep your mind sharp, relax, and something fun to do with limited time that you have. Do you think playing chess has made you a better football player? Has it made me a better football player? I don't know about that. The mental strategies are certainly similar as far as predicting, analyzing what your opponent is trying to do and counteracting that and finding the right balance between defense and attack. item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is reveling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the NWSL, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: 'They are the team to beat' - Anthony Gordon admits PSG were 'better' as Barcelona's 11-game winning streak ends in Champions League thriller
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-PSG-BARCELONA - AFP Anthony Gordon has delivered a remarkably candid assessment of Barcelona's high-stakes Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain, acknowledging that the reigning champions remain the gold standard in Europe. Despite a spirited display from the Catalan side, Gordon noted that their opponents possessed a level of sustained intensity that Hansi Flick’s men could not match over the full 90 minutes. PSG end Barcelona's flawless run Paris Saint-Germain brought Barcelona’s impressive 11-game winning streak to a crashing halt with a 4-2 victory in the Champions League . Flick had urged his squad to prove they belonged among Europe’s elite, and for large spells, the Catalan giants answered that call. Goals from Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal kept the hosts firmly in contention during a fiercely contested encounter. However, the back-to-back European champions ultimately showcased their pedigree, with late strikes from Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz securing the points and preserving PSG's flawless 100 per cent record in this year's competition. Gordon reflects on Parisian quality Speaking after the final whistle, Gordon offered a blunt evaluation of the match, conceding that the visitors simply outlasted their hosts. The forward felt that PSG’s physical conditioning and relentless pressure ultimately decided the contest. "I think they deserved it in the end. I feel like they were the better team," Gordon told TNT Sport . "They had better moments with more quality and I feel like athletically they were able to sustain the pressure, the intensity for longer than we were. They've been the team to beat for two years, tonight is a great example of why." FBL-EUR-C1-PSG-BARCELONA Work still to do for Flick's side Despite the setback, the defeat serves as a valuable measuring stick for a Barcelona side still developing under Flick. The squad remains eager to reach the lofty standards set by the Parisian outfit over recent seasons. "I think we can take great positives because we played well, it was a competitive spectacle," Gordon explained. "But we've still got work to do and I think that's a good position." Stressing the need for continuous improvement, he concluded: "They've been the best for two years, they're still the team to beat and we need to take from this that we need to do enough work, analyse this game and try and become that team. Try and become the team that needs to be beaten." Clasico redemption awaits FBL-EUR-C1-PSG-BARCELONA Barcelona have little time to dwell on their European disappointment as domestic duties quickly take precedence. Flick’s men face a massive test of their resolve when they take on fierce rivals Real Madrid in Sunday’s Clasico. Bouncing back immediately in Spain's biggest fixture will be crucial for the Catalan side to regain their momentum and put this Champions League setback firmly behind them.

item.title: Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya opens the door to a future move to Spanish football
item.description: Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya opens the door to a future move to Spanish football Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya has said he would 'love' to play in La Liga later in his career. Raya outlined his desire to return to Spain and play in La Liga, during an interview with Marca this week. The 31-year-old has evolved into one of Europe's top goalkeepers in North London, and helped Arsenal to Premier League title success last season. He has won the Premier League Golden Glove in three consecutive campaigns and has been nominated for the 2026 Yashin trophy, awarded to the best goalkeeper at the Ballon d'Or awards. A childhood Real Madrid fan, Raya has spent his entire professional career in England, after joining Blackburn Rovers’ academy as a 16-year-old. Asked whether he would like to test himself in La Liga, Raya said he was happy at Arsenal but would 'love' the opportunity later down the line. “Yes, I would love to. I would love to try out LaLiga. For now, I’m very happy here [at Arsenal], but I would certainly like to experience the Spanish league," he said. “I think it’s a very competitive league. Perhaps, in the future, I could play for a Spanish club. I’m Spanish, and I’d love to play there — that’s for sure.” Raya's current contract at Arsenal expires in 2028 and the Gunners could look to extend his terms to ward off La Liga interest. Arsenal have recently agreed a new deal for Mikel Arteta and are close to finalising terms with Declan Rice.
item.content:encoded: Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya opens the door to a future move to Spanish football Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya has said he would 'love' to play in La Liga later in his career. Raya outlined his desire to return to Spain and play in La Liga, during an interview with Marca this week. The 31-year-old has evolved into one of Europe's top goalkeepers in North London, and helped Arsenal to Premier League title success last season. He has won the Premier League Golden Glove in three consecutive campaigns and has been nominated for the 2026 Yashin trophy, awarded to the best goalkeeper at the Ballon d'Or awards. A childhood Real Madrid fan, Raya has spent his entire professional career in England, after joining Blackburn Rovers’ academy as a 16-year-old. Asked whether he would like to test himself in La Liga, Raya said he was happy at Arsenal but would 'love' the opportunity later down the line. “Yes, I would love to. I would love to try out LaLiga. For now, I’m very happy here [at Arsenal], but I would certainly like to experience the Spanish league," he said. “I think it’s a very competitive league. Perhaps, in the future, I could play for a Spanish club. I’m Spanish, and I’d love to play there — that’s for sure.” Raya's current contract at Arsenal expires in 2028 and the Gunners could look to extend his terms to ward off La Liga interest. Arsenal have recently agreed a new deal for Mikel Arteta and are close to finalising terms with Declan Rice.

item.content:encoded: theOBR CLEVELAND, OHIO ( TheOBR.com ) - Good morning, Cleveland Browns fans! THE DAILY BLOVIATION Across Cleveland, we have erected various memorials with local meaning. There’s a statue of Jim Brown in front of the stadium, which I used as a backdrop to the announcement that the OBR was going independent once more. There's a script “Cleveland” at a couple of locations celebrating something about the city. The fact that we have a name and are kind of retro, I guess. There are a bunch of guitars outside the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. There's a free stamp near City Hall, which I have yet to figure out. We need another one to celebrate the Browns' quarter century of searching for a quarterback. There’s already that uniform that appeared in a storefront in Cleveland recording the recurring pain of hope, but we need something celebrating the search itself. I propose a proud statue of Browns scout, complete with clipboard, stopwatch, and a confused look on his face looking outward over the Lake, representing the eternal quest to provide the Browns with a field general who will some day arrive, taking the town to the promised land of competitiveness. Then again, that might be expensive, and we all have to save up for PSLs at the new domed stadium. But it would represent the last 25 years+ of Browns football wandering the desert looking for a quarterback to fall from the sky to save our Sunday afternoons. This pain should be remembered by future generations of Browns fans, who can give up props through the decades for putting up with it. "A quarterback away" should be the city’s new slogan. We can build an identity around it. You know the history, of course. The Browns have started 42 different quarterbacks since 1999, by CBS Sports' count when Shedeur Sanders became the latest one last November. For most of those years, saying the Browns were a quarterback away was a kindness. We were a quarterback, a coach, a general manager, an offensive line and most of a defense away. The quarterback was just the part that fit in a headline. So I had mixed feelings when I saw ESPN's Ben Solak make it one of his "Seven things I think" this week: "I think... the Browns are a quarterback away from contending." Solak is upfront that it wasn't his idea. ESPN's Mina Kimes said it in August, when ESPN NFL posted her saying "[The Browns] really are a quarterback away" and asked if you agreed. We’ve asked the same question around here for months, but it’s our lot to be ignored by the Bristol colossus. Six weeks into the season, though, Solak says, "I'm there." His case starts with the young offensive talent: Quinshon Judkins, Harold Fannin Jr., and the rookie receivers, Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion. Then he gets to the quarterback, and he doesn't sugarcoat it. Game to game, he calls Deshaun Watson "one of the worst starting quarterbacks in the league." The numbers he uses aren't kind. Watson has the fourth-highest rate of interceptions plus sacks per dropback (11.8 percent), the third-worst explosive pass rate and the second-worst completion percentage over expected. Solak's summary: "not accurate, quick to worsen a muddy pocket and not nearly the same athlete on the move he was before two tears to his right Achilles tendon." He also breaks down a play from Sunday that I'll bet some of you are still mad about. It's 10-10 with 3:45 left, third-and-8. The speed out to Concepcion is there, and Solak says the ball "should be out to Concepcion every single time." Watson works the backside instead, nothing is open, and he barely escapes a sack. Then Andre Szmyt's 48-yarder goes wide left. We’re used to this sort of analysis around here. We watch the tape and even have Sam Penix provide a weekly accuracy chart. The results are not good. The part of Solak's column I enjoyed most is the defense, because he's right and he says so with feeling. "What a group!" This is a unit that lost Jim Schwartz and Myles Garrett in the same offseason, and Jared Verse, the headliner of the Garrett trade, has "underwhelmed relative to expectations." (Our Ask the Insiders crowd is already asking whether Verse is really playing as badly as everyone says.) Solak credits Schwesinger's "All-Pro blend" of quickness and processing speed, Maliek Collins on the interior, Quincy Williams playing like his old self under Mike Rutenberg, and a safety trio of Grant Delpit, Ronnie Hickman and Emmanuel McNeil-Warren. "Rutenberg's unit simply gets it." Solak does add an asterisk. Since Trevor Lawrence ripped them apart in Week 1, the Browns have faced Baker Mayfield, Bryce Young, Aaron Rodgers, Geno Smith and Tyler Huntley. Fair. But I notice the next three are Cam Ward, Rodgers again and Tyler Shough, and ESPN's own power rankings have Ward's Titans last in the league in passing at 153.3 yards a game. The asterisk can wait until November. Solak's closing line is "Good defense. Good offense. Someone get these guys a quarterback!" Two out of three, I'll buy. "Good offense" is generous. By Solak's own numbers, the Browns have the worst run game in football by success rate, and Watson faces the fourth-highest pressure rate of any quarterback. In those same ESPN power rankings, Daniel Oyefusi picks run blocking as the Browns' biggest offensive problem: 24th in run block win rate and dead last in yards before contact. Todd Monken said Monday the fix starts with him , "and then our offensive staff, and then the guys that we put on the field." My amendment: the Browns are a quarterback and an offensive line away. That's still a shorter list than I'm used to writing. ESPN's power panel, by the way, has the first-place Browns 19th. The 2-4 Rams are 14th. ESPN contains multitudes. So when does the quarterback show up? Not by the trade deadline, I'd bet. For 2026, it's Watson, and he's 4-2 with four fourth-quarter game-winning drives. He's also good at being a teammate. After Monken gave him a game ball Sunday, somebody yelled "party at your house," and Watson answered, as cleveland.com cleaned it up, "(H---) yeah, party at 4's house." He followed through Monday night, food trucks and all. "It's been a long 22 months, and this is what I did it for." The real answer comes in the spring. Watson's contract runs out, and we've been skeptical here that he gets another one . The Browns would currently pick 26th, plus No. 11 from the Rams, per Cabot. Over in the Watercooler, Brrexkl's Week 7 preview says it best: "LVR for the love of our LAR Draft Pick!" Solak doesn't mention the other quarterback on the roster, and today, neither will I. For the first time in a long time, the sentence ends at "quarterback." I'll take it. This and that, otherwise... JORDAN ELLIOTT: The Titans released former Browns defensive tackle Jordan Elliott on Tuesday after an "incident" at their facility. PFT rounds up the reports KPRC's Aaron Wilson and others: after an Oct. 15 argument with tackle JC Latham, Elliott was told to leave the practice field and went to the players' garage to get his gun from his car. Defensive tackle John Franklin-Myers de-escalated it. Nashville police said no reports had been filed. Elliott was a Browns third-round pick in 2020 and spent four years here. Thank goodness for John Franklin-Myers. The Titans' best defensive lineman is still there, and you'll hear a lot about him. Solak's pick for Defensive Player of the Year through six weeks is Jeffery Simmons, who leads all defensive tackles with 26 pressures. Our run blocking gets the test Sunday. FLEX DENIED: The NFL thought about moving Browns-Steelers to Sunday night in Week 8 and kept Eagles-Commanders instead , per the Inquirer's Rob Tornoe. That's a 2-4 team and a 1-4-1 team. The first-place Browns stay at 1 p.m. on CBS on Nov. 1. Respect remains a work in progress. FOREVER IS A LONG TIME: Jeremy Fowler reports the owners approved G5 financing for the Brook Park stadium, the league's loan program that goes up to $300 million. Meanwhile, Front Office

item.title: Russell Wilson names ‘very smart’ WR the Chiefs should trade for to help Patrick Mahomes
item.description: Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs remain unbeaten through their fifth game of the season at the weekend against the Los Angeles Chargers but something extra may be required for them before the trade deadline. There has been a lot of speculation surrounding the Chiefs and a potential wide receiver acquisition. Former Chiefs star Tyreek Hill has been one of the main names spoken about as he looks for his next team following his injury return. However, there may also be some questions as to whether Hill truly moves the needle for the Chiefs. With Kenneth Walker III essentially becoming the focal point of the Chiefs’ offence, another option at receiver may be needed to balance out that side of the ball. With the trade deadline just a matter of weeks away, Russell Wilson has named one star wide receiver he thinks could be perfect for Andy Reid’s team. Russell Wilson names Garrett Wilson as perfect WR trade for the Chiefs Through their opening five games of the season, Travis Kelce is leading the receiving yards for the Chiefs with 299. Considering Kelce only racked up 15 yards in the recent game against the Las Vegas Raiders, and still leads the tally, it goes to show how much room for improvement there is. “If I’m the Kansas City Chiefs, I got the all-star running back in the backfield, Kenneth Walker, which we’ve never had before. All these years, we’ve never had a running back like this running the ball the way he does. Guess what that does? That play action opens up. What Mahomes does better than arguably anybody in the world is throw the ball down the field,” said Wilson on CBS. “If I’m thinking about this, who would I go get? I’m going to go get Garrett Wilson. If the Jets keep losing, I’m going to go get Garrett Wilson from the New York Football Jets because I believe that. Garrett Wilson down the field with his ability. He’s a smart guy. He learns quickly. He’d be great in an Andy Reid-style offence. Patrick Mahomes, how he gets in and out of his breaks. They haven’t had a receiver like him. He’s very smart.”” Wilson has been able to catch for 418 receiving yards in what has been a struggling New York Jets team this season. The Jets are 2-4 and up against the Buffalo Bills and New England Patriots in the AFC East. Wilson is not going to enjoy any postseason football this year in New York. At the age of 26, the opportunity to play with Patrick Mahomes would surely be too good for Wilson to pass up. item.title: Bayern star to miss Arsenal game after sudden death of father
item.description: Bayern star to miss Arsenal game after sudden death of father One of Bayern’s most important players will now miss the Allianz Arena meeting on compassionate leave, while several other key figures are also unavailable or doubtful. Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images Bayern Munich will be without Joshua Kimmich against Arsenal tonight following the sudden death of his father, aged just 57. Kimmich had missed Tuesday’s training for ‘personal reasons’, but the initial expectation was that he would still be available for the Champions League meeting. Bayern have now confirmed that he will miss the match following the bereavement. Kimmich joins Michael Olise and Jamal Musiala among Bayern’s confirmed absentees. Olise is serving a one-match European suspension after receiving two yellow cards in Bayern’s 3-3 draw away to Viking . The former Crystal Palace star scored their third goal in Saturday’s 6-1 victory over RB Leipzig , taking his tally for the season to nine. Lennart Karl , who scored against Arsenal last season, is the favourite to replace him on the right. Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images Musiala is still recovering from the thigh tear suffered on international duty last month. Reports suggest he requires approximately another week, which would take his total absence to around a month, although that remains a provisional estimate rather than a confirmed comeback date. Ismael Saibari played as the number 10 against Leipzig and is expected to continue there. There is also uncertainty over Manuel Neuer . The goalkeeper has missed Bayern’s past two matches with a foot problem which sporting director Max Eberl described as “a bit of fluid on the foot”. Eberl said it was “nothing serious”, although it was still enough to keep Neuer out against Viking and Leipzig. The 40-year-old returned to training on Tuesday, putting him in contention for tonight. Jonas Urbig has deputised in Neuer’s absence and is ready to continue if required. Bayern could even be without their head coach on the touchline. Vincent Kompany has a viral infection that is causing him leg pain and missed Tuesday’s training session and press conference. Assistant Aaron Danks has handled preparations in his absence. Reports differ over whether Kompany will be able to attend tonight, so his involvement remains uncertain. Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images Bayern star to miss Arsenal game after sudden death of fatherOne of Bayern’s most important players will now miss the Allianz Arena meeting on compassionate leave, while several other key figures are also unavailable or doubtful. item.description: Joyce Edwards. | Getty Images Less than two weeks from the official start of the 2026-27 women’s college basketball season, the AP released its Top 25 preseason poll, with 31 voters providing an initial prognostication about how teams will stack up in the season ahead. Defending national championship UCLA, after seeing the departure of their six seniors, sit outside the top 10, ranked at No. 11. The top spot, instead, was claimed by South Carolina, with the Gamecocks garnering 23 of 31 possible first-place votes. 5th time in 7 seasons – Preseason #1 in both polls! 🔗: https://t.co/Cg2wMhSRU9 pic.twitter.com/bm5AHzgw1F — South Carolina Women's Basketball (@GamecockWBB) October 20, 2026 The remaining first-place votes were given to UConn, with the No. 2-ranked Huskies receiving six first-place votes, and USC. The Trojans, welcoming another No. 1 recruit in Saniyah Hall in addition to anticipating the return of JuJu Watkins, took the final two first-place votes as they start the season at No. 3 in the nation. always got each other's backs 🤞 on that training camp grind. pic.twitter.com/uHNdMkDRoB — USC Women's Basketball (@USCWBB) October 16, 2026 Asked about earning the preseason No. 1 ranking for the fifth time in the past seven seasons, South Carolina head coach Dawn Staley said : It’s a gift and curse. I tend to not look at the number, but our players do. They look at it and feel like there’s a sense of respect to being No. 1. They also know that it’s pressure-packed. With the type of nonconference schedule we have, we’re going to be challenged. If we stand there at No. 1 at the end of our nonconference season that’s something to be truly to be proud of. Staley’s Gamecocks are one of seven SEC teams that will begin the season ranked. The Big Ten, however, has the most ranked teams, totaling nine in the top 25. item.title: What’s next in Mets offseason? 2027 free agency, key dates and questions
item.description: It has been almost one month away from the diamond for the Mets. A calamitous 2026 season meant that the final day of the regular season back on Sept. 27 seemed like a foregone conclusion throughout the campaign. Uneven performance spelled a second straight postseason absence. The Mets front office has now had plenty of time to map out a plan for the offseason. The Mets locked up their manager in Andy Green late in the season and have added to their front office. A looming lockout may or may not get the ball rolling quicker on some movement once the World Series ends. With the official offseason right around the corner, here are some dates to watch and a few storylines for the Mets in the months before the 2027 season: When does MLB free agency start? Once the World Series concludes, the offseason begins and teams have a five-day negotiating window to try and retain their own players. Five days after the conclusion of the World Series, players can begin signing with other teams. The earliest the World Series could conclude would be after Game 4 on Oct. 27. Game 7, if necessary, is slated for Oct. 31. Who are Mets' free agents and will Bo Bichette opt in? After a transformative offseason that saw Edwin Diaz and Pete Alonso depart, the Mets do not have any unrestricted free agents as they approach the 2027 season. The one major question is whether Bo Bichette will return. The Mets third baseman has a $42 million player option for the upcoming campaign. He must make his decision on exercising that option within five days of the conclusion of the World Series. It is a sparse market for position players, adding some intrigue to Bichette's decision, but the 28-year-old is also coming off a down year. He posted a .702 OPS with 18 home runs, 78 RBI and 76 runs in his first season with the Mets. Will trio of Mets win Gold Gloves? item.content:encoded: It has been almost one month away from the diamond for the Mets. A calamitous 2026 season meant that the final day of the regular season back on Sept. 27 seemed like a foregone conclusion throughout the campaign. Uneven performance spelled a second straight postseason absence. The Mets front office has now had plenty of time to map out a plan for the offseason. The Mets locked up their manager in Andy Green late in the season and have added to their front office. A looming lockout may or may not get the ball rolling quicker on some movement once the World Series ends. With the official offseason right around the corner, here are some dates to watch and a few storylines for the Mets in the months before the 2027 season: When does MLB free agency start? Once the World Series concludes, the offseason begins and teams have a five-day negotiating window to try and retain their own players. Five days after the conclusion of the World Series, players can begin signing with other teams. The earliest the World Series could conclude would be after Game 4 on Oct. 27. Game 7, if necessary, is slated for Oct. 31. Who are Mets' free agents and will Bo Bichette opt in? After a transformative offseason that saw Edwin Diaz and Pete Alonso depart, the Mets do not have any unrestricted free agents as they approach the 2027 season. The one major question is whether Bo Bichette will return. The Mets third baseman has a $42 million player option for the upcoming campaign. He must make his decision on exercising that option within five days of the conclusion of the World Series. It is a sparse market for position players, adding some intrigue to Bichette's decision, but the 28-year-old is also coming off a down year. He posted a .702 OPS with 18 home runs, 78 RBI and 76 runs in his first season with the Mets. Will trio of Mets win Gold Gloves? While David Stearns might not be using the philosophy of "run prevention" any more following a disappointing 2026 season, there were a trio of Mets who lived up to the billing defensively. Luis Torrens, Carson Benge and Nolan McLean were named finalists for the Rawlings Gold Glove at their respective positions this season. Behind the plate, Torrens caught 10 runners stealing on 30 attempts and he notched a +5 blocks above average - tied for 10th best in MLB. Torrens' +12 defensive runs saved was third-best in MLB. Torrens is going up against the Padres' Freddy Fermin and Diamondbacks ' Gabriel Moreno. After a shaky start, Benge proved himself as one of the most capable defenders in the outfield in the National League. He closed with a +8 fielding run value while boasting the best arm value in all of baseball. His 10 outfield assists for tied for sixth-most in MLB. He is up against the Diamondbacks' Corbin Carroll and Cubs' Seiya Suzuki. McLean posted a +4 defensive runs saved from the mound. He converted 40 of his 43 defensive chances. The Mets rookie right-hander is a finalist along with the Braves' Chris Sale and Cardinals' Michael McGreevy. The finalists for the Silver Slugger Awards will be announced on Nov. 2, with the winners named on Nov. 17. Can Carson Benge win BBWAA Rookie of the Year? The National League Rookie of the Year figures to be one of the most closely contested races during the Baseball Writers Association of America's awards week. The run, which includes the Manager, Cy Young and MVP awards, opens with the top rookie being unveiled on Nov. 9. Benge offers the Mets with their best chance to take home any of the awards after he posted the Mets' first 20-20 season in 2026, while flashing dynamic defense. He slashed .282/.346/.430 with 20 home runs, 86 runs, 65 RBI, 22 stolen bases and 22 doubles in 156 games in his rookie season. The 23-year-old figures to see stiff competition from the Reds' Sal Stewart and Cardinals' J.J. Wetherholt for the award. McLean and the Rockies TJ Rumfield will also draw some consideration. When are Major League Baseball's GM meetings? The annual meeting of baseball's top executives will take place between Nov. 9 and 12 in Las Vegas. The potential for a looming lockout on Dec. 1, with the league's owners and the MLB Players Association negotiating a new labor agreement, adds further intrigue to this year's festivities. Also, the impact of that uncertainty on player negotiations before the turn of the new year will be fascinating, making this season's GM meetings more captivating than before. The owners will meet one week later in New York City as the clock ticks down on their current Collective Bargaining Agreement. Will Mark Vientos be given a contract? When is MLB non-tender deadline? The Mets have 10 players who are eligible for salary arbitration if they do not have a contract in place for the upcoming 2027 season. The non-tender deadline for teams to offer contracts to these players is Nov. 20. If players have not agreed to terms on a contract by mid-January, the players and his representatives and the team undergo an arbitration hearing in February to determine the terms of the contract. The Mets will have to decide whether to tender contracts to names like Mark Vientos, Austin Warren and Cionel Perez, who provide upside but do not have any minor league options remaining entering 2027. When are MLB's Winter Meetings? While Major League Baseball's Winter Meetings are in question based on the league's labor negotiations, it is slated for Dec. 7 through 10 in San Diego. A season ago, the Mets were the talk of the event after the departures of Diaz and Alonso were hatched at the event in Orlando. The top free agents heading into the offseason include Tarik Skubal, Randy Arozarena, Michael King, Clay Holmes, Seiya Suzuki and Jazz Chisholm Jr. Will Mets get a top pick in MLB Draft? When is the lottery? The MLB Draft Lottery is slated for Dec. 8 at the Winter Meetings, barring a work stoppage which would push it to a separate date. There is a great deal of intrigue for the Mets in this season's lottery. The Mets finished with the fifth-worst record in MLB and have a 62.6 percent chance to pick in the top six or 8.68 percent chance at the top pick. If the Mets' pick falls outside of the top six, it would drop 10 slots down the board due to the club breaching the luxury tax threshold When is the Rule 5 Draft and who could be picked from Mets? The Rule 5 Draft, which is held on the final day of the winter meetings, allows teams across the league to select players who have not been added to a team's 40-man roster within five seasons of the time of signing if they were 18 years old or younger or four seasons if they were 19 years old or older. The Mets have a number of players who they would need to add to the roster to ensure they're not open to be grabbed by another team this winter. That list includes Ryan Clifford, Jacob Reimer, Jefferson Rojas, Chris Suero, Marco Vargas and Jack Wenninger. When does Mets' 2027 spring training and season begin? The Mets are scheduled to play their first Grapefruit League game on Feb. 19 against the Marlins at Clover Park in Port St. Lucie, Fla. The Mets' regular season begins on the road in Miami, with Opening Day slated against the Marlins on Thursday, March 25. The Mets' home opener is Friday, April 2 against the Giants at Citi Field. item.title: PSG winger Kvaratskhelia suffers ACL rupture during win over Barcelona
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Paris Saint-Germain's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia celebrates scoring his side's first goal during the UEFA Super Cup final soccer match between Aston Villa and Paris Saint-Germain at Stadion Salzburg. (is associated with: «PSG winger Kvaratskhelia suffers ACL rupture during win over Barcelona») Adam Davy/PA Wire/dpa Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set for a long-term lay-off after rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament in Tuesday night's Champions League win over Barcelona. The European champions confirmed Kvaratskhelia, who received extensive treatment early in the second half of the 4-2 triumph at Parc des Princes following a challenge with Xavi Espar, will have surgery "in the coming days". A statement on PSG's website on Wednesday morning read: "Victim of a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during yesterday's match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia will undergo surgery in the coming days." The 25-year-old Georgia captain's injury setback is a major blow for PSG, who are in pursuit of a third straight Champions League crown. Kvaratskhelia has emerged as one of the world's leading forwards since joining the French champions from Napoli for in January 2025. PSG have been in scintillating form in Europe this season since defending their title in May, beating Manchester City and Barcelona by the same 4-2 scoreline this month. But Tuesday's latest victory has come at a cost as the club also confirmed that France forward Ousmane Dembele and captain Marquinhos will be out of action for "the coming weeks" due to thigh injuries.

item.title: Is Emma Aicher the top alpine skiing World Cup favourite?
item.description: Germany's Emma Aicher competes in the 1st round of the women's Giant Slalom race of the FIS Alpin Ski World Cup finals in Kvitfjell. (is associated with: «Is Emma Aicher the top alpine skiing World Cup favourite?») Cornelius Poppe/NTB/dpa Emma Aicher cannot hide that she is aiming for the overall World Cup title but still doesn't want to fuel expectations ahead of Saturday's start of the alpine skiing World Cup season. The 22-year-old came close last season when she challenged American great Mikaela Shiffrin until the end and only lost out by 87 points. Shiffrin has now said that she plans to focus mainly on super-g and giant slalom and won't contest every race in her pet event, the slalom, where she won nine out of 10 races last season for 900 of her 1,410 points. All-rounder Aicher That could open the door for the 22-year-old Aicher, who like last season plans to compete in every race across the disciplines which automatically makes her a contender again. ‘With four disciplines, it’s quite clear that this is a goal, I think. But in the end, you just have to put it out of your mind somehow," Aicher has said. "I want to focus on my own things – what I can do better, what I can do to get faster. I can’t influence the rest." Aicher could make an early impression in Saturday's season-opening giant slalom in Sölden, Austria. She has five World Cup victories from downhill and super-g races and podium finishes in slalom while she is yet to make the podium in giant slalom where fourth is her best result. More rivals than Shiffrin Aicher said that Shiffrin's reduced slalom schedule doesn't automatically make her the favourite because "there are so many other fast girls, regardless of the discipline. I must give my all to be in contention." Aicher's main plan remains unchanged - "skiing well and having fun" - an approach that earned her two Olympic silver medals in February and will also keep expectations in check this season highlighted by the world championships in Crans-Montana, Switzerland. First since Höfl-Riesch? Maria Höfl-Riesch is the last German woman to win the overall globe, in 2011, and she believes that Aicher has the quality to follow in her footsteps. "I am keeping my fingers crossed for her that it continues, that she stays healthy and that she plays a leading role again in the fight for the overall World Cup," Höfl-Riesch told broadcasters Bayerischer Rundfunk. Head coach Andreas Puelacher meanwhile shared Aicher's cautious approach, saying that "it is not easy to be top over the whole season" and pointing out that Shiffrin is a contender in all disciplines as well. Puelacher said it is impossible to plan such a title while Aicher's team-mate Kira Weidle-Winkelmann said that "this ease she has on her skis, and also a touch of the naivety in the way she goes about it" were a winning formula together with her talent and class. item.title: NC State vs. Stanford injury report: Duke Scott among many players out
item.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 20: Luke Mergott #34 of the Duke Blue Devils attempts to tackle Jayden Scott #4 of the North Carolina State Wolfpack during the first half of the game at Wallace Wade Stadium on September 20, 2025 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Has NC State’s injury situation improved after a week off? No, not really. In addition to missing at least two starting linemen, State will again be without running back Duke Scott, so that’s unfortunate. Not as unfortunate as the Pack’s dilapidated ground game, but not far off. Yousef Mugharbil joined the out-for-season list after the injury he suffered against Louisville, which is a bummer for a guy who has already been through a lot to get back to a point where he’s making an impact on the field. Jimarion McCrimon isn’t listed at all on the report this week, so that’s a positive development, but Kamen Smith is questionable again. Working with a patchwork line is a little easier against the likes of Stanford than Wake or Louisville, at least. Stanford’s most notable injured player is linebacker Matt Rose, who was a second-team All-ACC player in 2025 after racking up 106 tackles. He hasn’t played in a game for the Cardinal since the last week of September.

item.title: Matt LaFleur Has Strong Take About Jordan Love After Packers’ Win vs. Cowboys
item.description: Matt LaFleur had a strong endorsement for Jordan Love after the Green Bay Packers secured a 23-13 victory over the Dallas Cowboys. The head coach’s emphatic assessment reflected his confidence in the quarterback, who helped guide Green Bay to another important win. LaFleur used a brief but memorable description to express his admiration for Love’s performance. The coach’s praise highlighted the quarterback’s toughness and competitive mindset, qualities that have become increasingly important as the Packers continue building momentum. Green Bay’s latest victory also extended its winning streak to three games, strengthening the team’s position as the season progresses. Sep 7, 2025; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) during the game against the Detroit Lions at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Love’s performance against Dallas came as the Packers relied on a balanced effort to control the game. Although the offense did not need to carry the entire burden, the quarterback remained central to Green Bay’s ability to manage possessions and capitalize on opportunities. His presence under center continues to give the team confidence in its ability to compete against quality opposition. Green Bay’s defense also played a significant role in the victory, limiting the Cowboys to 13 points and helping prevent Dallas from generating enough offense to threaten the outcome. The unit’s performance complemented the offense and demonstrated how the Packers can succeed without relying exclusively on explosive passing plays. That balance could prove valuable as the team faces tougher challenges later in the campaign. This can be seen in a video shared by the league’s official Instagram account. View this post on Instagram A post shared by NFL (@nfl) “He’s a G,” Matt LaFleur said. “We talk about playing like a G. item.title: Newcastle Red Bulls sign Canada lock Flesch
item.description: Mason Flesch in action for Canada against the USA in the Pacific Nations Cup in September [Getty Images] Newcastle Red Bulls have signed Canada forward Mason Flesch until the end of the season. The 26-year-old - who can play at lock or in the back row - has been capped 26 times by his country. Flesch scored 10 tries in 11 games for Chicago Hounds, including one in the final as his side overcame California Legion to claim the Major League Rugby title and was named the league's forward of the season for 2026. Ontario-born Flesch came through the ranks with the Toronto Arrows and made his professional debut in 2021 before winning his first Canada cap later that year. Head coach Dan McFarland told the Newcastle website: "Mason has been a stand-out performer in Major League Rugby and for his country, and deserves this opportunity. "He is a great athlete who will add depth to a very competitive area of our squad, and I look forward to working with him in our environment." Flesch, who arrived on Tyneside this week, added: "I'm incredibly excited to be a part of this team. "I'm looking forward to being involved with a quality full-time organisation, and most importantly very eager to train and help push standards." Newcastle have lost their first three Prem games this season and also lost their European Challenge Cup opener 47-14 at Scarlets last Saturday.

item.title: Kansas City Chiefs Announce History After Week 6

His latest accomplishment highlights his consistency and importance to a defense that continues to play a central role in the team’s pursuit of success. Bolton reached a significant franchise benchmark during Kansas City’s win over the Los Angeles Chargers , reinforcing his reputation as one of the unit’s most dependable players. The achievement reflects his ability to remain productive across multiple seasons while handling the responsibilities that come with being a key figure in the middle of the defense. His impact extends beyond individual statistics, particularly when the Chiefs need leadership and discipline in critical situations. His instincts allow him to react quickly against both the run and the pass, while his physical approach helps Kansas City maintain its defensive intensity. Those qualities have made him a valuable part of the team’s structure and helped him build a reputation for reliability. The Week 6 victory also demonstrated how important defensive execution can be when the Chiefs face challenging opponents. Limiting scoring opportunities, making timely stops and forcing offenses into difficult situations can change the course of a game. Bolton’s achievement provides another reminder that Kansas City’s success is not solely dependent on its offensive stars, as defensive contributors continue to establish their own place in franchise history. item.content:encoded: Jack Munro (L) and Richard Livornese (R) win their 7th straight Men's Doubles pro title on the APP. APP The Association of Pickleball Players (APP) held its eighth domestic full points event of the 2026 season this past weekend, and became the first pro tour to ever play an event in Kentucky, with the 2026 Humana APP Louisville Open. The tour played this event at the Kentucky International Convention Center in downtown Louisville, and its players got to visit all the attractions that Louisville is known for. Click here for the PickleballDen.com home page for the event , where you can get tournament details, draw sheets, and results. News and Noteworthy ahead of the Event Here’s a quick recap of notable news items of import to the tour or this event: 10/8/26: APP announces its fy2027 slate of domestic events , featuring 12 events (one a month) around the country. new sites for 2027 include Palm Beach Gardens, and an Arizona spot in December; the rest are returning core events from the 2026 slate. 9/22/26: The APP announces the APP Moneyball Series . APP Moneyball Series is a new competitive series for current and aspiring professional pickleball players, offering high-level local competition, prize money, APP Tour ranking points, and a pathway to national and global events. With that said, let’s recap the action. Men’s Pro Singles Recap Men’s Singles on the APP continues to show parity, with 6 distinct winners in the last 9 events held. The winner from the last event (Tristan Dussault) was upset in the round of 16 by Jake Bower, and five of the eight top seeds in the draw failed to advance to the quarters. However, the final ended up being 1v2, with the tour’s top ranked player Ronan Camron taking out No. 2 Dusty Boyer for his 3rd career singles title. Veteran Eduardo Irizarry pipped Bower for the Bronze. Gold : Ronan Camron. Silver : Dusty Boyer. Bronze : Eduardo Irizarry. Women’s Pro Singles Recap After several events of chaos in the Women’s singles draw, this one went almost completely chalk from beginning to end. The only interloper double-digit seed into the quarters was Australian Roos van Reek (who’s talents are not matched by her seed), who fell at that juncture to fellow No. 4 seed Aussie Seone Mendez. From there, the top players on tour battled it out in the semis and finals to great effect. No. 1 Stewart went three games and edged Mendez 11-9 in one semi, while No. 2 Domenika Turkovic also had to dig deep to top No. 3 Oshiro. In the final. Turkovic got her second APP singles title in a row with a 3-game upset win over Stewart to close the gap at the top of the rankings. Gold : Domenika Turkovic. Silver : Kat Stewart. Bronze : Bobbi Oshiro. Mixed Pro Doubles Recap One of the “fun” things that happen when a player of the quality of Jay Devilliers suddenly parachutes into a tour is the propensity for very low seeds to make very big runs. In mixed, Devilliers paired with Domenika Turkovic to create a very formidable, but very under-seeded Mixed team. They met the top seeds in the round of 16 in No. 1 Megan Fudge & Aiden Schenk, and moved past them with relative ease 6,4. In fact, Devilliers & Turkovic made it all the way to the final, with multiple additional upsets along the way. In the final, they ran into the tour’s top ranked Mixed Male player in Jack Munro, playing this week with the visiting Australian Roos van Reek, and they made the most of the trip, beating Jay & Domenika for gold. Gold : van Reek & Munro. Silver : turkovic & Devilliers. Bronze : Stewart & Livornese. Men’s Pro Doubles Recap The Men’s doubles draw was shaken early, when the No. 2 seeds Palm & Camron were ousted in the first round by Shay Hugo & Kevin Caulfield. This opened up an opportunity on the bottom half for the veteran No. 15 seeds Naveen Beasley & Max Wild, and they made a run to the semis before falling. However, it was all for naught, as the top seeds Jack Munro & Richard Livornese Jr. were not to be denied. The No. 1 seeds won their 7th straight APP Men’s Doubles draw, beating No. 3 Aidan Schenk & Zack Marceau in the final. Jay Devilliers & Tanner Tomassi, silver medalists in Columbus two weeks ago, salvaged the bronze. Gold : Munro & Livornese. Silver : Schenk & Marceau. Bronze : Devilliers & Tomassi. Women’s Pro Doubles Recap Kat Stewart (L) and Bobbi Oshiro (R) cruised to the Women's Doubles title. APP On the backs of two gold medals in the last few events, Shelby Bates & Christine Maddox have taken over the No. 1 team spot on tour, but they ran into the buzz saw that is Glauka Carvajal Lane lately. She’s taken three straight APP/APP International silver medals lately, with three different partners. In Kentucky, Lane paired up with Domenika Turkovic, with whom she won silver in Columbus two weeks ago, and they took out the top seeds in the semi to push for another gold. In the final, they met No. 3 Bobbi Oshiro & Kat Stewart, who took out the under-seeded No. 10 pair of Vivian Glozman & Roos van Reek in dominant fashion in the bottom semi. In the final, it was another bridesmaid day for Lane and Turkovic, losing 2,9 for another silver medal. Kat Stewart finishes the event with 3 medals: a Gold, a Silver, and a Bronze. Gold : Oshiro & Stewart. Silver : Lane & Turkovic. Bronze : Bates & Maddox. AARP Champions Pro Competition Quick Recap Men’s Champions Pro Singles: APP No. 1 Youssef Bouzidi crushed No. 2 Marcello Jardim for the title, the 9th time in the last 10 Champions pro singles draws these two met for gold. Women’s Champions Pro Singles: With the APP No. 1 Karin Ptaszek-Kochis missing, newcomer and shoe-in for Rookie of the Year Carolina Lopez Ascarate dominated Lee Whitwell for gold. Men’s Champions Pro Doubles: Youssef Bouzidi made it a double, teaming with Dayne Gingrich to win the Doubles title as the top seeds. Women’s Champions Pro Doubles: The two singles finalists, Ascarate & Whitwell, teamed up to cruise to the Doubles title together. Mixed Champions Pro Doubles: Carolina Lopez Ascarate/Marcello Jardim took the mixed title as the No. 2 seeds, securing the triple crown for Carolina Lopez Ascarate for the weekend, her first. AARP Masters 60+ Pro Competition Quick Recap Men’s Masters 60+ Pro Singles: Adam Painter took the Singles 60+ as the No. 3 seed. Men’s Masters 60+ Pro Doubles: APP 60+ newcomers Rich Lively & Ross Weinberg shocked the field and took the title. Shoutout to Weinberg, a Virginia native and an old racquetball colleague of mine from years ago here in the state. Women’s Masters 60+ Pro Doubles: Ginny Purdy & Heather Iffert ( did double duty also playing Champions pro this weekend) took the 60+ Women’s doubles title. Mixed Masters 60+ Pro Doubles: Heather Iffert got the 60+ pro double by winning Mixed with Mark Wilder. The Pro Pickleball Medal Tracker spreadsheets have now been updated with these results. Click here for the Pro-only Medal Tracker , and click here for the Senior Pro Medal Tracker . These spreadsheets hold Medal winners for every pro event going back to the beginnings of the tours. Next up on the Pickleball Calendar? According to my Master Pickleball Schedule , Next up for the APP is the 2026 Dubai Open this coming weekend. They also have Next and Collegiate events over the next couple of weeks, and then more international events planned in Mid November. Their next domestic tournament is 11/15 weekend in Arizona. item.title: Christopher Nkunku ‘can imagine’ staying at RB Leipzig
item.description: Christopher Nkunku ‘can imagine’ staying at RB Leipzig Christopher Nkunku (28) has struck four goals and provided two assists in eight appearances across all competitions since returning to RB Leipzig on loan from Serie A outfit Milan. Gearing up ahead of Wednesday’s UEFA Champions League clash against Real Madrid, the Frenchman stated that he could imagine staying at the Saxony club beyond his current loan, which expires in June 2027. “I’m very happy,” Nkunku told Sport Bild . “I feel very comfortable in the city and at the club. Of course, I can very well imagine staying longer.” During his first spell at Leipzig between 2019 and 2023, the Frenchman registered 47 goals and 43 assists in 119 Bundesliga appearances before departing for Chelsea. “I had some very significant moments in my career and my life in Leipzig and with RB,” he explained. “I really enjoyed those four years. But, above all, the clubs would have to reach an agreement at the end of the season, so it’s not just up to me.” GGFN | Daniel Pinder
