item.title: ‘You shouldn’t be able to represent the USA’: Riley Gaines not happy as WNBA players skip national anthem
item.description: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect The Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries have drawn plenty of criticism from conservative corners of the internet after both teams left the court before the national anthem during the first two games of the WNBA Finals. Now, one of the WNBA’s most vocal critics has weighed in. Anti-trans activist and former Kentucky swimmer Riley Gaines suggested that players who kneel for the anthem should be barred from playing for Team USA at the Olympics. It’s a very aggressive argument from Gaines, but there’s just one problem: nobody actually knelt during the national anthem. Teams Leave Court for Anthem Before Game 1 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday, both teams were warming up at Chase Center before they left the court shortly before the anthem . They then jogged back onto the floor just seconds after it ended. The same thing happened again before Game 2 on Monday night, according to Fox News . Neither the teams nor the league has explained why the players left the court. OutKick has pointed to the WNBA’s rulebook, which calls for players, coaches, and trainers to stand in a line during the anthem. But that rule only appears to apply if the players are on the court, and it doesn’t seem to require them to be there in the first place. It’s also not clear whether the moment was intentional. Leaving the floor at a set time before tipoff isn’t uncommon in basketball, and LSU head coach Kim Mulkey gave a similar explanation in 2024 when her team, which included current Dream star Angel Reese, was off the court for the anthem before an Elite Eight game against Iowa. ‘You shouldn’t be able to represent the USA’ Gaines shared her take on X on Tuesday while quote-posting a clip of the teams leaving the court before Game 2. “It’s my personal opinion that if you kneel for the flag and what it represents, you shouldn’t be able to represent the USA at the Olympics,” Gaines wrote . The post went viral, racking up tens of thousands of likes. But it’s worth noting that Gaines’ criticism wasn’t necessarily based on reality, as the players did not actually kneel during the national anthem, they just weren’t on the floor at all. Gaines has become one of the WNBA’s most prominent critics in recent months, particularly when it comes to transgender athletes in women’s sports . Ever since tying transgender swimmer Lia Thomas for fifth at the 2022 NCAA Championships, Gaines has built a platform speaking out against transgender women competing in women’s sports. She now hosts The Riley Gaines Show for OutKick, which was rebranded from Gaines for Girls in January to cover broader political commentary. This month, she has also been touring college campuses with Turning Point USA . The post ‘You shouldn’t be able to represent the USA’: Riley Gaines not happy as WNBA players skip national anthem appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan Indicates Trade Stance After Concerning Development
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers keep on winning . In fact, they have not tasted defeat so far in the 2026 NFL season, as they improved to 6-0 after thwarting Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders in Week 6’s 23-17 win at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara on Monday. But the Niners are not without problems. For one, they have an unenviable situation in their wide receiver room, with plenty of hurt bodies in the group. Star wide receiver Mike Evans just aggravated an Achilles issue in the Commanders game, and it forced him to leave the contest in the first half. He was unable to return to the game, though, he still ended up leading all San Francisco players with 94 receiving yards on three receptions and five targets. Will The 49ers Address Their Wide Receiver Situation With a Big Trade? Sep 11, 2026; Melbourne, Victoria, Australia; San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (5) at press conference after the 2026 NFL Melbourne Game against the Los Angeles Rams at Melbourne Cricket Ground. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Apart from Evans, the Niners also have Ricky Pearsall, De’Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson, Deebo Samuel Sr. and Christian Kirk, all with injury designations. All those players sat out the game against the Commanders. Some of them could potentially return sooner rather than later, but as it stands, San Francisco’s wide receiver unit is far from its best shape. A trade could help ease the problem in the group for San Francisco, but an acquisition via that route doesn’t seem likely at the moment. Via Nick Wagoner of ESPN : All of that attrition would seem to set the stage for a trade, though Shanahan indicated the team might stick with what it has for another week and then see where things stand after the bye. Nevertheless, San Francisco’s offense has been among the most prolific in the league, putting up 29.5 points and 366.7 total yards per game, both top 10 in the league to date. Coming up next for the Niners is a Week 7 game against the Atlanta Falcons on the road. Sep 14, 2025; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan looks at the score board as he leaves the field at the end of game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images Related content Kirk Cousins Accidentally Destroys Photographer’s Equipment During Raiders-Bills Game Klint Kubiak Knows What Needs to be Fixed With Raiders After Loss to Bills Colts’ Jonathan Taylor Knows ‘No One is Coming to Save’ Indianapolis Amid 2026 Struggles Old Video of Cardinals’ Mack Wilson Resurfaces After Taking Down The Rams in Week 6 The post 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan Indicates Trade Stance After Concerning Development appeared first on Gridiron Heroics .

item.title: Post-Wuhan WTA Power Rankings: Rybakina Leads, But Who Is Her Biggest Threat?
item.description: Tennis - U.S. Open - Flushing Meadows, New York, United States - September 12, 2026 Kazakhstan's Elena Rybakina celebrates with the winner's trophy after her final match against Belarus' Aryna Sabalenka IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters/Robert Deutsch | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jim Smith The WTA season is nearing its conclusion, and the landscape looks quite different from what we saw in our pre-Wimbledon WTA power rankings . Elena Rybakina has established herself as the dominant player of 2026, Linda Noskova has become a Grand Slam champion, Mirra Andreeva continues to make extraordinary progress, and Aryna Sabalenka has experienced an unexpected decline. Meanwhile, Maja Chwalinska has emerged as one of the season’s most remarkable stories, following her Roland Garros final with an unlikely Wuhan Masters title. As always, these are not simply the WTA rankings. They combine season-long accomplishments, recent form, consistency, performances against elite opposition, and the level each player can produce heading into the final stretch. Players currently sidelined by injury, including Amanda Anisimova, are excluded. With the WTA Finals approaching, here is the updated order. Post-Wuhan WTA Power Rankings 1. Elena Rybakina WTA Ranking: No. 1 Previous Power Ranking: 2 There is no serious argument against Rybakina occupying the top position in the WTA power rankings. The Kazakhstani has won the Australian Open and US Open, defeating Sabalenka in both finals, and earned 7,503 Race points. Her 6-4 5-7 6-2 victory over Sabalenka in New York was particularly impressive, securing her third Grand Slam title and ultimately the world No. 1 ranking. Rybakina’s serve remains arguably the most effective weapon in women’s tennis, while her flat, powerful groundstrokes allow her to dictate rallies without relying on spectacular defensive movement. However, her recent physical problems cannot be ignored. A recurring foot and lower-leg issue contributed to her Cincinnati retirement and subsequent withdrawal from Wuhan. She also suffered a surprising opening-round defeat to Alina Charaeva in Beijing. She is scheduled to return in Ningbo, but her fitness remains the biggest question heading into the WTA Finals. If healthy, she is the obvious favourite. 2. Mirra Andreeva WTA Ranking: No. 3 Previous Power Ranking: 3 Andreeva’s first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros was already enough to establish 2026 as the most important season of her career. But the 19-year-old has continued improving. Her run to the Beijing final demonstrated that her success in Paris was hardly a one-off, even if Qinwen Zheng eventually defeated her 7-5 6-4. Andreeva now sits third in the Race with more than 6,300 points. Her greatest strength remains her remarkable tactical understanding. She can absorb pace, redirect shots and disrupt opponents without taking unnecessary risks. However, her US Open quarter-final defeat to Coco Gauff exposed an area that still needs improvement. Andreeva led 6-2 and

Andreeva led 6-2 and held two match points in the second-set tiebreak before losing in three sets. Those setbacks are part of her development, but they also prevent her from challenging Rybakina for the top position. Still, she might be the most complete young player on Tour. 3. Linda Noskova WTA Ranking: No. 8 Previous Power Ranking: 9 Noskova arrived at Wimbledon after winning the Berlin title, but few would have predicted she would leave London as a Grand Slam champion. The Czech defeated Karolina Muchova 6-2 5-7 6-3 in the final, completing an extraordinary grass-court season. She then reached the US Open quarter-finals, pushing Sabalenka to three sets before narrowly losing. Noskova’s powerful serve and aggressive groundstrokes make her particularly dangerous when conditions reward first-strike tennis. Unlike some players with similar weapons, however, she has become increasingly comfortable constructing points rather than simply attempting to hit through opponents. Her game still has inconsistencies, and her recent Asian swing has not been especially impressive. Nevertheless, winning Wimbledon and Berlin in the same season deserves enormous recognition. At 21, Noskova has already accomplished something most players never will, earning her spot at No. 3 in the WTA power rankings. 4. Aryna Sabalenka WTA Ranking: No. 2 Previous Power Ranking: 1 Sabalenka’s decline is one of the season’s more surprising developments. She began 2026 by winning 26 of her first 27 matches, completing the Sunshine Double and looking almost unbeatable. Since Miami, however, her results have deteriorated considerably. The Belarusian has not won another title and has lost two Grand Slam finals against Rybakina. Her latest defeat against Ann Li in Wuhan was really worrying. Sabalenka led 6-3 4-2 before losing 3-6 6-4 7-6, committing 44 unforced errors in another match that slipped away from a winning position. The problem is not a lack of weapons; it never was. Her serve, return and aggressive groundstrokes remain among the best on Tour. But her error management has deteriorated, and she has repeatedly struggled to maintain control after establishing an advantage. Sabalenka’s ceiling remains extraordinarily high. Right now, however, her consistency does not justify a higher position in the WTA power rankings. 5. Coco Gauff WTA Ranking: No. 5 Previous Power Ranking: 8 Gauff has enjoyed an encouraging second half of the season. Her Cincinnati title was very impressive, culminating in a victory over Jessica Pegula in the final. She followed that success by reaching the US Open semi-finals, where her remarkable comeback against Andreeva demonstrated why she remains one of the toughest competitors in women’s tennis. Her defensive movement remains exceptional, while improvements to her serve have made her considerably more competitive on hard courts. However, she still has occasional problems with her forehand, especially when opponents consistently attack that side. Those vulnerabilities prevent her from producing the same relentless baseline pressure as Rybakina or Sabalenka at their best. Still, she has qualified for another WTA Finals and deserves consideration as a serious contender. 6. Jessica Pegula WTA Ranking: No. 4 Previous Power Ranking: 5 Pegula remains one of the most reliable performers on the WTA Tour. She has won titles in Dubai and Charleston, reached the Cincinnati final, and qualified for another WTA Finals appearance. Her consistency is impressive. She rarely relies on overwhelming power. Instead, she takes the ball early, redirects pace and uses excellent court positioning to pressure opponents. Her ability to maintain a high baseline level makes her extremely difficult to beat. However, the same question still follows her. Can she produce enough exceptional tennis to defeat the very best players across several consecutive matches? Her Cincinnati defeat to Gauff was disappointing, while a second-round loss to Jelena Ostapenko in Wuhan did little to improve her recent form. Pegula remains a credible threat, but she is not currently playing quite well enough to challenge the leading contenders in the WTA power rankings. 7. Maja Chwalinska WTA Ranking: No. 11 Previous Power Ranking: NR Perhaps the most remarkable story in women’s tennis this season . Chwalinska entered Roland Garros as a qualifier and somehow reached the final, eventually losing to Andreeva. That achievement alone would have been extraordinary. But the Polish player has now added a WTA 1000 title in Wuhan. Her run included a 7-5 6-1 semi-final victory over Iga Swiatek before she recovered from a set down to defeat Sonay Kartal 2-6 6-4 6-2 in the final. Chwalinska does not have the overwhelming power of some players. Her game relies on intelligent shot placement, variation, and the ability to disrupt opponents’ preferred patterns. item.title: Here’s how the Browns have a Chance for not only a Winning Record, but a Playoff Spot
item.description: theOBR BEREA, Ohio — Former NFL coach Jim Mora famously was asked after a loss if his Colts team could still make the playoffs. His answer became a famous meme. “’Playoffs? Don’t talk about—playoffs? You kidding me? Playoffs?! I just hope we can win a game! Another game!” Don’t look now, but the Browns are 4-2 (2-0 AFC North). Despite not playing well on offense on a regular, consistent basis, the offense has been able to score when needed, to get wins in four, fourth quarter games. No matter how they got to 4-2, their record is what it is and it has put them in position to do some things that were not imagined by most before the season started. The Browns have not been in first place in the division this late in the season, since the 2014 season, when they were 6-3 after nine games. Unfortunately that season, the Browns went 1-6 the rest of the way that season, finished 7-9 and missed the playoffs. Currently, the Browns would make the playoffs as the division winner, due to tiebreakers. They would be the No. 4 seed in the playoffs and host a first-round game. The only two teams in the AFC with better records than the Browns are the Chiefs (5-0) and the Bills (5-1). The Jaguars lead their division at 4-2, while the Patriots, Broncos, Steelers and Ravens are all 4-2. We thought the Browns would win between five and nine games, if everything went right for them. We picked them to be 6-11. To get to nine wins, they had to have average to above average quarterback play—and to this point, they have. With 11 games to play, the Browns could play below .500 the rest of the way and still have a winning record. A 5-6 record in the final 11 games gets the Browns to 9-8. To put that into perspective, the Browns have only had four winning seasons since the team returned in 1999: 2002 (9-7), 2007 (10-6), 2020 (11-5) and 2023 (11-6). They've made the playoffs three times, 2002, 2020 and 2023, all three as a wild card team. The Browns have never won the AFC North. The last time they won their division was in 1989, when it was the AFC Central. When told the betting odds before the season had the Browns winning 5 1/2 games, owner Jimmy Haslam said he would take the ‘over’ during training camp. If the Browns go 6-5 the rest of the way, they would finish 10-7, likely being in the mix for a playoff spot, either as the winner of the AFC North or as a wild card team. To put that into perspective, the Browns have only had four winning seasons since the team returned in 1999: 2002 (9-7), 2007 (10-6), 2020 (11-5) and 2023 (11-6). They've made the playoffs three times, 2002, 2020 and 2023, all three as a wild card team. The Browns have never won the AFC North. The last time they won their division was in 1989, when it was the AFC Central. When told the betting odds before the season had the Browns winning 5 1/2 games, owner Jimmy Haslam said he would take the ‘over’ during training camp. If the Browns go 6-5 the rest of the way, they would finish 10-7, likely being in the mix for a playoff spot, either as the winner of the AFC North or as a wild card team. Currently, six AFC teams are 2-4 or worse, leaving 10 of the remaining 16 teams in the AFC in contention. Seven teams make the playoffs, including four division winners and three wild card teams. According to The Providence Journal , NFL teams that start a season 2-4 manage to make the playoffs, only 9-19 percent of the time. The long-term historical rate (since 1990) found that of the 205 NFL teams that started 2-4, only 9.3 percent of those teams made the playoffs. The recent trend, since playoffs were expanded to seven teams in both conferences in 2020, the success has been higher. About 19 percent of teams that started the season 2-4 made the playoffs. The most recent team to start 2-4 and make the playoffs was the Titans in 2019, who started 2-4 and finished with a 9-7 record. Of the 16 AFC teams, six have records of 2-4 or worse. Although teams have turned it around before after a 2-4 start, the odds are only 9-19 percent of making the playoffs, likely leaving 10 teams fighting for seven playoff spots. With that said, here are the records of the teams the Browns have on their schedule the rest of the way and their current records. @ Titans (1-5) @ Steelers (4-2) @ Saints (2-4) Texans (2-4) Raiders (3-3) Bengals (3-2) Falcons (2-4) @ Giants (3-2-1) @ Ravens (4-2) Colts (2-4) @ Bengals (3-2) Only five of the games are against teams, currently with a winning record. Four of those five games are in the AFC North. The only teams on the schedule with a winning record that is not in the AFC North is the Giants, who are currently 3-2-1. The overall record for the teams the Browns play the rest of the way is 29-34-1 for a winning percentage of .461. According to the website, Tankathon.com , the Browns have the fifth-easiest schedule remaining in the NFL. Eleven games is a long way to go in the NFL and things can go sideways quickly, as Browns fans know so well, but there is hope for the Browns and the journey continues on Sunday against the 1-5 Titans.

item.title: Indiana football’s defense is still championship-level, as shown by the Ohio State game
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, IN - SEPTEMBER 25: Indiana Hoosiers Defensive Coordinator Bryant Haines prior to a college football game between the Northwestern Wildcats and Indiana Hoosiers on September 25, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Indiana’s heavyweight bout with Ohio State this past weekend taught us a few things about this team. One of the most important lessons came from the defense, which looked like a another championship unit despite the loss to the Buckeyes at home. Bryant Haines is the best assistant coach in college football and he has the hardware to prove it as last season’s Broyles Award winner. As long as he’s with the program, the Hoosiers will have a strong defense. He’s done more great work with this group. Indiana had to replace cornerstones like Aiden Fisher, Mikail Kamara, D’Angelo Ponds and Louis Moore, among others, in building out this group. This new unit leans on Isaiah Jones and Rolijah Hardy at linebacker with freshman Jacob Savage showing he can play right away alongside them. Jamari Sharpe slid up as Indiana’s No. 1 cornerback with Penn State transfer AJ Harris taking over at No. 2. Wisconsin transfer Preston Zachman took over at safety while Byron Baldwin slid up at rover. Amare Ferrell stayed put and remains as vital as ever. Indiana’s defensive interior of Tyrique Tucker and Mario Landino remains as good as ever with Tulsa transfer Joe Hjelle and freshman Blake Smythe proving impactful as well. The additions of Tobi Osunsanmi and Chiddi Obiazor along with the late retentions of Stephen Daley and Kellan Wyatt have proven stout as well. Indiana had a lot to replace. It did so about as well as it could’ve. The secondary took some heat early on this season with some warning signs in non-conference play and against Northwestern but that group, as its predecessors did in 2025, has tightened up and played better in recent weeks, especially as Harris has returned to the lineup. The result of all this was holding Ohio State to its lowest scoring output of the season up to this point. The Hoosiers managed four sacks, six and a half tackles for loss and a pair of interceptions out of the Buckeyes in keeping the game close as the offense worked to figure out its own issues with Ohio State’s defense. Indiana even managed to largely contain Jeremiah Smith’s impact of the game. Between exploiting Julian Sayin’s reliance on Smith to going after the quarterback, the Hoosiers limited the star wide receiver to four receptions and 68 yards. Outside of a lone blown coverage in the endzone (a huge deal! yes! but!), Indiana kept Smith from doing too much damage. If Indiana can do that to Ohio State, it can do so to just about anyone. The Hoosier defense kept that 2025 team in games against Iowa, Oregon, Penn State and Ohio State itself while the offense figured out what it needed to do to win. This year’s offense needs to do this year’s defense t

item.title: Do you know why Harry Kane is poised to make history at the Ballon d’Or?
item.description: (Photo by Reinaldo Coddou H./Bundesliga via Getty Images) | Bundesliga via Getty Images Bayern Munich has known its fair share of legendary strikers. Harry Kane follows in the footsteps of giants, from Gerd Müller to Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, from Giovane Élber and Luca Toni to Robert Lewandowski in the most recent past. Few won the biggest individual prize football has to offer. One was arguably robbed (twice!). In the coming days, Kane stands a chance of cementing himself in history. His record speaks for itself. Seventy-three goals last season means he will be awarded the Müller Trophy, given to the highest scorer from the past season. This will be the England captain’s second time winning the award, with both instances coming after his move to FC Bayern in 2023. In this case, club and player have found a winning combination that elevates each other. So, what accolades await the 33-year-old at the Ballon d’Or ceremony? Well, let’s recap: He will become the second player to win two Müller Trophies, following in the footsteps of Robert Lewandowski, who also did it with Bayern Munich. He could become the first Ballon d’Or winner who also won the Müller Trophy the same year. Both Erling Haaland and Robert Lewandowski had a shot, but they never got the big prize due to extenuating circumstances. He could become the fourth Bayern Munich player to win the Ballon d’Or, after Gerd Müller, Franz Beckenbauer, and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge. In the same vein, he would become the seventh player to lift the Ballon d’Or while playing for a Bundesliga club. Following on to that stat, he would become the fifth English player and the seventh British player to win a Ballon d’Or. He follows in the footsteps of Kevin Keegan, who also played in the Bundesliga, and Michael Owen, the last Englishman to lift the trophy for his country. Of course, all this supposes that Kane actually does win the Ballo n d’Or this year. He seems to be the favorite for the oddsmakers, but FC Barcelona and Spain youngster Lamine Yamal b oasts a strong claim thanks to his country winning the World Cup. Real Madrid and France striker Kylian Mbappé has also put his name in for contention, though he falls short of Kane on goals, and Yamal (plus Kane) on trophies. Lest we forget Michael Oli se, Kane’s teammate, who had an incredible season of his own. For Harry Kane, this ceremony could represen t the pinnacle of personal achievement—the exact thing he was looking for when he left Tottenham Hotspur back in 2023. If the judges chosen by France Football make the right choice, the England striker could add his name to an illustrious list, sol idifying his legacy as one of the greatest strikers in the sport.lustrious list, solidifying his legacy as one of the greatest strikers in the sport. item.title: Travis Kelce’s Kansas City teammate says ‘if I had a son, I’d want him to be just like him’
item.description: Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images Kansas City Chiefs TE Travis Kelce is not only a legend on the field, but he is also a shining example of a good man to his teammates off the field. The 36-year-old Kelce has established himself as one of the most respected veterans in the NFL, hoping to win a fourth Super Bowl title with the Chiefs in the 2026 season. One of the key reinforcements the Chiefs made to their roster after a 6-11 season in 2025 was rookie CB Mansoor Delane, who they selected with the No. 6 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. Despite playing on opposite ends of the field, Kelce has left an impact on Delane. Mansoor Delane wishes his unborn son grows up to be like Travis Kelce In a mic’d-up moment from the Chiefs’ Week 6 22-6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers, rookie CB Delane was caught on audio praising his veteran teammate, wishing that if he had a son, he would grow up to be like Kelce. “If I had a son, I’d want him to be just like him. He’s got so much aura, bro” Kelce has been a model leader in the Chiefs’ locker room, with his work ethic and continued success setting a fantastic example for the young players. His success on and off the field also explains why a 22-year-old like Delane would want to have a son like him. But with Kelce being a world-famous athlete who is a multimillionaire and considered a gentleman, it’s hard to question anyone who says they want their son to be like Kelce. Kelce has picked up 20 receptions for 299 yards this season and has converted two touchdowns in a season where his connection with Mahomes is no longer required to be the driving force behind the Chiefs’ success. Delane has been a standout defensive rookie for the Chiefs, playing four games for 22 tackles (15 solo, seven assisted), two TFLs, one interception, and three passes defended. item.title: Sophie Cunningham questions Angel Reese’s play during the WNBA postseason
item.description: Source: lev radin/Shutterstock.com galecophoto/Depositphotos Cunningham questions Reese’s physical play Sophie Cunningham’s comments about Angel Reese’s physical play during the 2026 WNBA playoffs sparked debate about player safety and officiating. On her No Hesitation podcast, Cunningham discussed several incidents from the Atlanta Dream’s semifinal series against the New York Liberty, including exchanges involving Sabrina Ionescu and Jonquel Jones. Reese also played a key role in Atlanta’s sweep, scoring 22 points in the decisive Game 3 victory. The discussion highlights differing views on physical play, competitive intensity, and the consistency with which officials should enforce the rules. Depositphotos Reese helped Atlanta reach the WNBA Finals Atlanta defeated New York 85–83 in Game 3 of the semifinals on October 9, completing a three-game sweep. Reese scored 22 points in the deciding game at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, helping Atlanta reach the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013. The Dream entered the championship series unbeaten in the 2026 postseason after winning their first five playoff games. lev radin/Shutterstock.com Cunningham acknowledged Reese’s loyalty to teammates Cunningham did not dismiss Reese’s competitive approach entirely during the podcast discussion. She praised the Atlanta forward for supporting her teammates and noted that her intensity reflected care for those around her. However, Cunningham drew a distinction between standing up for a teammate and actions she believed could endanger opponents. Her criticism focused on specific plays rather than Reese’s effort alone. galkin57/Depositphotos The Sabrina Ionescu confrontation drew attention One incident involved New York Liberty guard Sabrina Ionescu during the decisive semifinal game. After Ionescu was called for an offensive foul on a screen involving Atlanta guard Isobel Borlase, Reese followed Ionescu down the court and appeared to address her. Cunningham argued that the interaction should have resulted in a technical foul against Reese, although officials did not assess one. Dziurek/Depositphotos Cunningham questioned the technical foul decision Cunningham said she believed Reese should have received a technical foul for following Ionescu and speaking directly to her after the whistle. She argued that similar conduct would ordinarily draw a penalty during the regular season or other playoff games. The officials did not issue a technical foul to Reese for that exchange, making the decision a central point in Cunningham’s public criticism. steho/Depositphotos Jonquel Jones and Reese received technical fouls Another heated moment occurred after New York center Jonquel Jones blocked Reese’s shot near the basket. The two players exchanged words and made chest-to-chest contact before officials intervened. Both players received technical fouls during the game, according to the game recap. The Dream entered the championship series unbeaten in the 2026 postseason after winning their first five playoff games. lev radin/Shutterstock.com Cunningham acknowledged Reese’s loyalty to teammates Cunningham did not dismiss Reese’s competitive approach entirely during the podcast discussion. She praised the Atlanta forward for supporting her teammates and noted that her intensity reflected care for those around her. However, Cunningham drew a distinction between standing up for a teammate and actions she believed could endanger opponents. Her criticism focused on specific plays rather than Reese’s effort alone. galkin57/Depositphotos The Sabrina Ionescu confrontation drew attention One incident involved New York Liberty guard Sabrina Ionescu during the decisive semifinal game. After Ionescu was called for an offensive foul on a screen involving Atlanta guard Isobel Borlase, Reese followed Ionescu down the court and appeared to address her. Cunningham argued that the interaction should have resulted in a technical foul against Reese, although officials did not assess one. Dziurek/Depositphotos Cunningham questioned the technical foul decision Cunningham said she believed Reese should have received a technical foul for following Ionescu and speaking directly to her after the whistle. She argued that similar conduct would ordinarily draw a penalty during the regular season or other playoff games. The officials did not issue a technical foul to Reese for that exchange, making the decision a central point in Cunningham’s public criticism. steho/Depositphotos Jonquel Jones and Reese received technical fouls Another heated moment occurred after New York center Jonquel Jones blocked Reese’s shot near the basket. The two players exchanged words and made chest-to-chest contact before officials intervened. Both players received technical fouls during the game, according to the game recap. Cunningham said she wished neither player had received a technical foul, describing the exchange as part of competitive playoff basketball. galecophoto/Depositphotos Cunningham raised concerns about player safety Cunningham also discussed physical plays involving Reese and opposing players during the semifinal game. She objected to what she described as actions directed toward opponents’ knees and ankles, as well as contact involving a player in the air. Cunningham characterized those types of plays as dangerous, presenting her concerns as a matter of player safety rather than simply competitive trash talk. Interesting fact : Sophie Cunningham played college basketball at the University of Missouri . Featureflash/Depositphotos Breanna Stewart was involved in another disputed play New York Liberty forward Breanna Stewart was involved in another play discussed by Cunningham and Drew Hanlen on their podcast. Cunningham criticized Reese for bumping Stewart to the floor after the play had ended. She also questioned why officials did not call a foul on that contact. Her comments were part of a broader discussion about the consistency of officiating during Atlanta’s semifinal series against New York. Interesting fact : The Atlanta Dream set a franchise scoring record in June 2026. katatonia82/Depositphotos Officiating consistency became part of the debate Cunningham’s remarks extended beyond whether Reese should have received a technical foul for confronting Ionescu. She questioned why officials penalized some exchanges but allowed other physical interactions to continue without a similar call. Her argument centered on consistent enforcement of the rules throughout a game. The discussion did not establish that officials had formally admitted to making an error on either play. steho/Depositphotos Reese delivered a strong performance in Game 3 Despite the attention surrounding the disputed plays, Reese also made a significant contribution to Atlanta’s victory. She scored 22 points in the deciding game as the Dream defeated the Liberty 85–83. Her performance helped Atlanta complete the three-game sweep and reach the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013. The victory secured the Dream’s place in the championship series after an unbeaten start to the 2026 postseason. livephotosport/Depositphotos Atlanta completed a three-game semifinal sweep The Dream won the opening game of the semifinal series 92-82 on October 4, then took Game 2 by a score of 101-98 on October 7. Their 85-83 victory in Game 3 completed the sweep against New York. Atlanta’s run ended the Liberty’s postseason campaign and sent the Dream into the championship round with a 5-0 playoff record. galecophoto/Depositphotos The Dream advanced to face the Valkyries Atlanta’s semifinal victory set up a WNBA Finals matchup against the Golden State Valkyries. Golden State also swept its semifinal series, defeating the defending champion Las Vegas Aces to reach the championship round in its second season. The Finals began on October 17, 2026, giving both franchises an opportunity to pursue their first WNBA championship. Michael Porter Jr.’s comments have drawn attention to the ongoing conversations surrounding Cunningham and her role with the Indiana Fever. Explore Michael Porter Jr. sharing a pointed message about Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham . Mircea Moira/Depositphotos Cunningham’s comments kept Reese in the spotlight Cunningham’s podcast remarks brought renewed attention to Reese’s physical style of play just before Atlanta’s championship series. Her comments addressed specific incidents, including exchanges with Ionescu and Jones, as well as broader concerns about contact and officiating. Reese’s postseason production and Atlanta’s successful run remained important parts of the story, while Cunningham’s criticism represented her assessment of the plays rather than an official league ruling. Indiana faces important roster questions as the franchise prepares for the next stage of its WNBA campaign. Find out how Sophie Cunningham’s free agency leaves Indiana Fever weighing key offseason decisions . What do you think about Sophie Cunningham’s criticism of Angel Reese’s physical play and the officials’ decisions? Like this post and share your opinion in the comments. item.title: Yankees Castoff Joins Hated Rival Immediate After Season Ends
item.description: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - APRIL 29: A view of the New York Yankees logo on a ball bag before the game against the Baltimore Orioles at Oriole Park at Camden Yards on April 29, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) Getty Images The New York Yankees are entering an important winter after another disappointing postseason exit, and the organization’s options for significant change just shrunk after it officially brought manager Aaron Boone back for another season. Attention now turns toward the possibility of big roster changes that can help New York get further into October next year after a particularly painful end to the Yankees’ season. “Boone is coming off one of the biggest disappointments of his tenure as Yankees manager — an embarrassing three-game sweep by the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division Series,” Brendan Kuty and Chris Kirschner noted for The Athletic . And while the Yankees consider how to improve their major-league roster, one player who was cast off at the beginning of the ill-fated campaign has already secured his next opportunity with an American League East rival. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Mets’ $17 Million Castoff Sends 5-Word Yankees Message New York Yankees Castoff Signs With Division Rival Baltimore Orioles Left-hander Jayvien Sandridge has agreed to a minor-league contract with the Baltimore Orioles for the 2027 season, according to Matt Weyrich of The Baltimore Sun . Sandridge’s return to Baltimore marks another turn in a winding professional journey. The Orioles originally selected him in the 32nd round of the 2018 MLB Draft, and he spent time in their organization before moving through the Cincinnati Reds, San Diego Padres and Yankees systems. New York designated Sandridge for assignment in January 2026 and traded him to the Los Angeles Angels for cash considerations. The Angels later designated him for assignment as well, and Baltimore acquired him in another cash deal in March. “Sandridge, 28 in February, began 2026 on the Yankees’ roster,” Darragh McDonald wrote for MLB Trade Rumors . “He was designated for assignment in January and then flipped to the Angels for cash. The Halos designated him for assignment at the end of spring training. That led to another cash deal, this one sending him to Baltimore.” The new agreement keeps Sandridge with the Orioles organization after an injury-shortened 2026 campaign. He made six relief appearances for Triple-A Norfolk before landing on the injured list in early May. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) Getty Images The New York Yankees are entering an important winter after another disappointing postseason exit, and the organization’s options for significant change just shrunk after it officially brought manager Aaron Boone back for another season. Attention now turns toward the possibility of big roster changes that can help New York get further into October next year after a particularly painful end to the Yankees’ season. “Boone is coming off one of the biggest disappointments of his tenure as Yankees manager — an embarrassing three-game sweep by the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division Series,” Brendan Kuty and Chris Kirschner noted for The Athletic . And while the Yankees consider how to improve their major-league roster, one player who was cast off at the beginning of the ill-fated campaign has already secured his next opportunity with an American League East rival. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Mets’ $17 Million Castoff Sends 5-Word Yankees Message New York Yankees Castoff Signs With Division Rival Baltimore Orioles Left-hander Jayvien Sandridge has agreed to a minor-league contract with the Baltimore Orioles for the 2027 season, according to Matt Weyrich of The Baltimore Sun . Sandridge’s return to Baltimore marks another turn in a winding professional journey. The Orioles originally selected him in the 32nd round of the 2018 MLB Draft, and he spent time in their organization before moving through the Cincinnati Reds, San Diego Padres and Yankees systems. New York designated Sandridge for assignment in January 2026 and traded him to the Los Angeles Angels for cash considerations. The Angels later designated him for assignment as well, and Baltimore acquired him in another cash deal in March. “Sandridge, 28 in February, began 2026 on the Yankees’ roster,” Darragh McDonald wrote for MLB Trade Rumors . “He was designated for assignment in January and then flipped to the Angels for cash. The Halos designated him for assignment at the end of spring training. That led to another cash deal, this one sending him to Baltimore.” The new agreement keeps Sandridge with the Orioles organization after an injury-shortened 2026 campaign. He made six relief appearances for Triple-A Norfolk before landing on the injured list in early May. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Dodgers Veteran Backstop Cuts Ties With Team Immediately After Season Ends Former New York Yankees Pitcher Looks For New Chance With AL East Rival Sandridge has limited major-league experience to draw on. He made his MLB debut with the Yankees on July 5, 2025, against the New York Mets, recording two outs while allowing two earned runs. His minor-league record offers a more complicated picture. The left-hander has demonstrated strikeout ability, but control has been a recurring concern, making his next opportunity dependent on both his health and his ability to limit walks. For Baltimore, the minor-league deal represents a low-risk way to retain a left-handed arm with some swing-and-miss potential. Sandridge will have to earn his way back into the major-league picture, rather than receiving a guaranteed roster spot. For the Yankees, his return to a division rival is a modest offseason footnote rather than a major roster blow. Still, with New York looking to move beyond its latest playoff disappointment, even smaller personnel moves help illustrate how quickly former Yankees can find new opportunities elsewhere in the division. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: KIRK SPEAKS: Minnesota
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 09: Jeremy Hecklinski #10 of the Iowa Hawkeyes celebrates a touchdown against the Washington Huskies during the first half at Husky Stadium on October 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before we jump in to this week’s edition of Kirk Speaks, a quick shout out to our usual author Matt Cabel who welcomed in the newest addition to his household a week earlier than expected. Everyone is doing great, except for those of us who sit around waiting for him to digest these weekly pressers for us. So congrats to Matt and family – we’ll do our best to fill the void! Happy Floyd week, folks. The bye is behind us, the Hawkeyes sit at 5-1 and #15 in the country at the exact halfway point of the season and the biggest question in Iowa City got itself answered on a Tuesday afternoon: Jeremy Hecklinski is the starting quarterback Saturday at Minnesota. What I love most is HOW the news came out. Monday’s depth chart had the dreaded “OR” between Hank Brown and Hecklinski, everybody spent 24 hours reading tea leaves, and then Kirk just… mentioned it. Mid-answer. Almost to himself. The man has guarded quarterback decisions like state secrets for a quarter century and this one he dropped like he was reading a grocery list. Let’s get into the details. You can check out the full transcript HERE , my highlights and commentary below. Q. I think we know how much equity matters to you within the program, the day-by-day work. You have two quarterbacks that have gone on the road in tough environments and pulled out wins. Whoever you go with at quarterback on Saturday, how do you balance continuing to instill confidence in them but also understanding that, as you’ve mentioned, you have depth at quarterback. I don’t want to use the phrase is the leash going to be shorter if they don’t perform, but how do you kind of maintain that balance of instilling confidence and maybe looking to make a change? KIRK FERENTZ: We’ll handle that as we go. Did I put up the depth chart? So Hecklinski will be our starter Saturday. Since the start of the season, it’s been even. What’s good for us is they’ve both done good jobs and both won on the road in tough circumstances. So that gives us a lot of encouragement. I think we have two good quarterbacks, which a couple years ago we couldn’t say that. “Did I put up the depth chart?” is an all-time way to announce your starting quarterback. item.content:encoded: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 09: Jeremy Hecklinski #10 of the Iowa Hawkeyes celebrates a touchdown against the Washington Huskies during the first half at Husky Stadium on October 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before we jump in to this week’s edition of Kirk Speaks, a quick shout out to our usual author Matt Cabel who welcomed in the newest addition to his household a week earlier than expected. Everyone is doing great, except for those of us who sit around waiting for him to digest these weekly pressers for us. So congrats to Matt and family – we’ll do our best to fill the void! Happy Floyd week, folks. The bye is behind us, the Hawkeyes sit at 5-1 and #15 in the country at the exact halfway point of the season and the biggest question in Iowa City got itself answered on a Tuesday afternoon: Jeremy Hecklinski is the starting quarterback Saturday at Minnesota. What I love most is HOW the news came out. Monday’s depth chart had the dreaded “OR” between Hank Brown and Hecklinski, everybody spent 24 hours reading tea leaves, and then Kirk just… mentioned it. Mid-answer. Almost to himself. The man has guarded quarterback decisions like state secrets for a quarter century and this one he dropped like he was reading a grocery list. Let’s get into the details. You can check out the full transcript HERE , my highlights and commentary below. Q. I think we know how much equity matters to you within the program, the day-by-day work. You have two quarterbacks that have gone on the road in tough environments and pulled out wins. Whoever you go with at quarterback on Saturday, how do you balance continuing to instill confidence in them but also understanding that, as you’ve mentioned, you have depth at quarterback. I don’t want to use the phrase is the leash going to be shorter if they don’t perform, but how do you kind of maintain that balance of instilling confidence and maybe looking to make a change? KIRK FERENTZ: We’ll handle that as we go. Did I put up the depth chart? So Hecklinski will be our starter Saturday. Since the start of the season, it’s been even. What’s good for us is they’ve both done good jobs and both won on the road in tough circumstances. So that gives us a lot of encouragement. I think we have two good quarterbacks, which a couple years ago we couldn’t say that. “Did I put up the depth chart?” is an all-time way to announce your starting quarterback. No statement, no graphic, just Kirk wondering aloud what’s on his own two-deep. Then casually announcing something completely counter to that depth chart after confirming it’s been put out. Wild, wild sequence and genuinely shocking that he announced anything at all. I’ve been pretty confident if Heck got the nod it would be under the guise that Hank Brown, while medically cleared and available as an emergency backup, was not fully back and needed more time. WELP…. Q. What is it that led you guys to the decision to start Jeremy? And then also is Hank at 100 percent? How is he doing health-wise? KIRK FERENTZ: Hank is 100 percent. He could have played the last game, emergency, but I don’t think it was a smart play to play him, and probably would have – not endangered him or they wouldn’t have cleared him, but probably would have set him back for a while. He’s perfectly healthy. A little sore last week, and having that bye week came at a good time. As a determining factor, it’s kind of like the first time. It’s not a coin toss, but it’s awfully close. Both guys, you can make an argument either way that makes sense. We just decided that was the best thing at this time to do, and we’ll just keep playing forward here. This part is maybe more baffling than Kirk just blurting it out. Brown is healthy – fully, 100 percent healthy, per KF – and the job went to Heck anyway. That makes this a performance call, not an injury bridge and that’s a big deal given where Iowa’s offense has been this season. When someone asked the question even more directly, Kirk made Brown’s case for him – “do you discount a quarterback bringing us back for two touchdowns in the fourth quarter?” – which tells you how close this really was . But close only counts in horseshoes. Heck’s the guy. Completing 79% of your throws against Power 4 defenses will do that for a guy. Q. Was curious with Xavier Styles, how you’ve seen him kind of develop since he got on campus and what he did to earn that starting opportunity? Also, I know you said Tyler Brown is out. Styles, do you expect him to start again versus Minnesota? KIRK FERENTZ: Kind of ties in with what Tom asked earlier about who’s going to — we’ve liked Xavier. Didn’t think he was ready. Anyway, with Tyler out, we have to find an answer. He and Anthony have both been competing. We just made that decision that last game to throw him in there and see what he’d do. He really flashed at some good things. Some detail work to take care of, which is what you’d expect any time a new player goes in. He’s only been here however many months, ten months on campus, so he’s still has some finer things. His knowledge base compared to like Zach Lutmer’s is a little bit different. Like his attitude and the way he runs around. He made a good showing for himself that first time out, so we’ll keep building on that. We’re going to keep working with Anthony too because he’s going to be a good player. The thing that both those guys are fighting is newness to the system and just all the intricate details. Luckily, we’ve got Zach back there to help quarterback some stuff and carry some of that burden. We liked what we saw. Just even standing on the sidelines a couple weeks ago, just him flashing around, you can just get a feel sometimes, like this guy is trying to make some plays and get involved and be active. Be curious to see where it goes. It’s all in front of him right now. Same thing with Anthony. He’ll get his chance. This feels like another one of Kirk’s meandering non-answers, but I think it roundabout highlights what makes Phil Parker’s defense click. We see the same basic defense that is predictable but there are details and intricacies that are nuanced and barely noticeable to the untrained eye. And the critical piece is everyone executing their role without the need to process. That’s a tough ask for a young guy and getting reps for so many of these younger players should pay big dividends down the road. Just hope it doesn’t bite the Hawks against quality QBs – Minnesota’s Drake Lindsay is capable of making Iowa pay for mistakes in the back end. Q. Also, when they went to Purdue, you could tell there was almost an it’s just Purdue kind of attitude with the way they played. What kind of message do you tell them and how they evaluate the film and the results in order to prepare them for this game? KIRK FERENTZ: One side thought, the just Purdue thing, which is kind of a commentary on last weekend. When my kids were all younger, it’s the old – I was guilty of the same thing when I was a little kid. When you play Little League games, right? The Cubs beat the Tigers, and then the Tigers beat the Reds, hey, we beat the Tigers, so we’ll naturally beat this team, and you end up losing by 10 runs. That kind of thinking gets you beat. Then the bigger picture is last weekend is a great illustration, if anyone is paying attention – I’m thinking more about our players than everybody else – but it’s just week to week because you can’t make it make sense if you do comparative scores. The Little League transitive-property bit is Kirk at his Kirkiest. The annoying part is he’s right. Minnesota beat the two ranked teams it played and got blown out by two unranked ones, so comparative scores are useless here. He also got in a swipe at the sport’s December brain – the “playoff shows coming out sometime in the next four weeks” – and said the best advice he can give his guys is to just worry about Saturday. We, of course, are unde

item.title: Future Hogs Week 7: College football players who could help the Commanders
item.description: LUBBOCK, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 18: Amare Thomas #0 of the Houston Cougars runs with the ball during the second half of the game against the Texas Tech Red Raiders at Galaxy Stadium on September 18, 2026 in Lubbock, Texas. (Photo by John E. Moore III/Getty Images) | Getty Images What an unpredictable week in college football. #1 Georgia lost to an unranked Auburn team, and #2 Notre Dame lost late to #8 BYU. #3 Miami needed overtime to beat in-state rival Florida State. #4 Ohio State won a competitive matchup over #5 Indiana, handing them their first loss at home under head coach Curt Cignetti. #6 Alabama lost by a wide margin in Knoxville to #14 Tennessee, and #7 Texas gave up a lead and lost to unranked Florida. This chaos has resulted in no undefeated SEC teams, UCLA as the only unbeaten team in the Big Ten, and three undefeated Big 12 teams – BYU, Texas Tech, and Utah – in the top 10. Week 8 will see one of those unbeaten teams in the Big 12, #10 Utah, facing off against #14 Houston. A new entrant into the top 10, #9 UCLA will host Michigan State. Both #13 Alabama and #17 Texas will try to avoid three losses in a row. The Crimson Tide will play Texas A&M while the Longhorns play #7 Ole Miss. The top team in the country, Miami, will host Pittsburgh. Here are a few players who had a good week and might be able to help out the Commanders. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to post players that stood out to you. Ashton Daniels | QB | Senior | Florida State As a developmental quarterback prospect, Ashton Daniels could be a fit in Washington. He’s got the size for the position at 6’2”, 225 pounds. He’s not the most creative runner at the position, but he can run away from, and at that size, even over defenders. As a passer, Daniels has shown the ability to make NFL-level throws between defenders and into tight windows. He also can put touch on his passes and allow receivers to run underneath them. He can get himself into trouble when he tries to force throws thinking he can beat defenders. Daniels has thrown 8 interceptions this season. If the Commanders think they can help him improve his decision making, he might be worth investing in. In an overtime loss to Miami, Daniels went 15 of 28 for 298 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception on the last play of the game which any Florida State fan will argue was a catch. He also added 31 yards and a touchdown on the ground. As a bonus for those who want a big receiver, check out Daniels’ teammate, the 6’6”, 230 pound wide receiver Duce Robinson, in the clip below. He’s wearing #0. DeSean Bishop | RB | Senior | Tennessee Many hoped that Kaytron Allen would be the Commanders’ short yardage back. That didn’t happen. DeSean Bishop can be that and more. He isn’t a flashy runner that will wow you with elite speed, burst, or elusiveness. What Bishop is at 5’10”, 215 pounds is a rugged back that will deliver consistent punishment to a defense, wearing them down as the game progresses.

(Photo by John E. Moore III/Getty Images) | Getty Images What an unpredictable week in college football. #1 Georgia lost to an unranked Auburn team, and #2 Notre Dame lost late to #8 BYU. #3 Miami needed overtime to beat in-state rival Florida State. #4 Ohio State won a competitive matchup over #5 Indiana, handing them their first loss at home under head coach Curt Cignetti. #6 Alabama lost by a wide margin in Knoxville to #14 Tennessee, and #7 Texas gave up a lead and lost to unranked Florida. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to post players that stood out to you. He’s not the most creative runner at the position, but he can run away from, and at that size, even over defenders. As a passer, Daniels has shown the ability to make NFL-level throws between defenders and into tight windows. He also can put touch on his passes and allow receivers to run underneath them. He can get himself into trouble when he tries to force throws thinking he can beat defenders. Daniels has thrown 8 interceptions this season. If the Commanders think they can help him improve his decision making, he might be worth investing in. In an overtime loss to Miami, Daniels went 15 of 28 for 298 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception on the last play of the game which any Florida State fan will argue was a catch. He also added 31 yards and a touchdown on the ground. As a bonus for those who want a big receiver, check out Daniels’ teammate, the 6’6”, 230 pound wide receiver Duce Robinson, in the clip below. He’s wearing #0. DeSean Bishop | RB | Senior | Tennessee Many hoped that Kaytron Allen would be the Commanders’ short yardage back. That didn’t happen. DeSean Bishop can be that and more. He isn’t a flashy runner that will wow you with elite speed, burst, or elusiveness. What Bishop is at 5’10”, 215 pounds is a rugged back that will deliver consistent punishment to a defense, wearing them down as the game progresses. His superpower is his ability to run through tackles and gain tough yardage, a role the Commanders need filled desperately. As a former walk-on, it is easy to root for Bishop’s success at the next level. Bishop rushed 32 times for 159 yards and two touchdows in the Volunteers’ victory over Alabama. DeSean Bishop’s Ranks Among RBs from Week 7: 🟠 121 Yards AFTER Contact (1st) 🟠 13 Missed Tackles Forced (1st) @Vol_Football pic.twitter.com/FF2lIwJgit — PFF College (@PFF_College) October 18, 2026 Amare Thomas | WR | Senior | Houston It was tough to see Terry McLaurin sustain a torn patellar tendon against San Francisco. The injury makes the need to improve the position group more urgent than it already was. Houston’s Amare Thomas is a receiver who could really improve the receiving corps. The 6’0”, 205 pound wideout is a quick-twitch athlete who can create separation with his route running. His superior body control and above-average hands allow him to make catches outside the frame of his body. After the catch, Thomas has contact balance to break arm tackles. Long speed is a bit of a question. Thomas helped Houston outlast Oklahoma State with seven catches for 126 yards and two touchdowns. Houston WR Amare Thomas is an NFL WR playing in the Big 12 He had a huge week 7 vs Oklahoma State with 7 receptions, 127 yards, and 2 TDs The size (6'0 205), body control, route running, and ability after the catch remind me of DJ Moore pic.twitter.com/Bs0lBaqgSS — Draft Capital Podcast (@TheDraftCapital) October 19, 2026 Peter Clarke | TE | Senior | Temple I talked about Peter Clarke during this time last year and it looks like he has gotten better. He’s a huge player at 6’6”, 265 pounds, and he uses that size in a variety of ways. First, it allows him to be an effective blocker at the line of scrimmage. Clarke looks like he has improved his technique and is getting lower to maintain leverage. He’s also added more to his game as a receiver. There’s more diversity to the routes he runs, but he still shows the quickness and speed of a smaller player. Clarke became Temple’s all-time touchdown leader for tight ends in a loss to Charlotte with 123 yards and a touchdown on five catches. Peter Clarke with a record breaking touchdown 🥳 📺 | @ESPNCFB #BuiltToRise x @Temple_FB pic.twitter.com/HqSFrMMPEV — The American (@American_Conf) October 17, 2026 Temple TE Peter Clarke ( @iam_peterclarke ) had his best game last week vs UConn. Clarke caught 5 passes for 88 yards and a TD. #TempleTUFF pic.twitter.com/2yQ3LlxZaa — Bryan (@RealBGauvin23) October 17, 2026 Justin Evans| C | Senior | Nebraska The offensive line had its fair share of struggles against the 49ers. Justin Evans looks like an immediate upgrade at the center position. He has a compact, powerful body at 6’2”, 315 pounds. Evans snaps the ball and gets his hands onto defenders quickly. He is stout in pass protection, constantly moving his feet to mirror rushers. Evans has a solid anchor to prevent power rushers from going through him to get to the quarterback. One of my favorite traits of his is he’ll constantly look for defenders to block. In the run game, he’s not a people mover. What he’ll do is identify defenders and sustain his block. Nebraska used a power run game, so Evans may not be a great fit for a zone rushing attack. Nebraska suffered a close loss on the road to Oregon, but #51 below had a good game. item.content:encoded: BLOOMINGTON, IN - OCTOBER 17: Indiana Hoosiers running back Turbo Richard (1) lines up behind the line of scrimmage in the second half of play during a college football game between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the Indiana Hoosiers on October 17, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images One of Indiana football’s supposed strengths just two weeks ago has emerged as perhaps its biggest weakness after a pair of lackluster showings. The Hoosiers’ running game looked great two games into Big Ten play. Indiana ran for 6.8 yards per carry as a team against Northwestern with Lee Beebe Jr. taking over for an injured Turbo Richard, logging 203 yards on 24 carries to average 8.5 on the ground in large part thanks to a 70-yard burst in the fourth quarter. It looked even better the next week when the Hoosiers averaged 8.4 yards per carry with Richard turning 13 carries into 204 yards for a blistering 15.7 yards per carry. Ever since? Nothing remotely close. Windy conditions made the run crucial at Nebraska and the Cornhuskers knew it, committing extensive resources to stopping the Hoosiers on the ground. Indiana, which had seen two different backs eclipse 200 rushing yards in the previous two weeks, managed just 65 rushing yards as a team and just 3 yards per carry against that defense. On top of that, Indiana lost the time of possession battle and just didn’t run that many offensive plays. It was a combination of Josh Hoover’s arm and processing alongside Nick Marsh’s playmaking that won that game. This seemed a potential outlier at the time. Weird game, weird weather. Whatever. Then came the massive matchup against Ohio State at home where Indiana ran into the same issue, literally. The Hoosiers managed just 73 yards on the ground and just 2.5 per carry against the Buckeyes as Turbo Richard finished with 46 and Beebe Jr. with 24. Neither were explosive, with their longest rushes on the game being tied at just seven yards. Despite the criticism he’s received, including from this very blog, it was Hoover that kept Indiana in position to win that game at the end. Indiana’s running game was doing it no favors. So, what gives? How did Indiana go from this explosive attack to looking pedestrian at best in just two weeks? It isn’t a talent issue in the backfield. Richard and Beebe Jr. have both proven capable, this very season and in the past, of putting together strong performances on the ground. Their individual performances against Northwestern and Rutgers weren’t fools gold, that was just players making plays. To really break this down you have to go back to this past offseason when Indiana reloaded its backfield through the transfer portal and returned a key piece from injury. Mike Shanahan and Curt Cignetti’s offense has changed some over the years as different players have come and gone and it’s certainly been friendly for quarterbacks, but everything starts with the run. That’s just football in general, but humor me for a moment. Indiana’s rushing attack in 2024 and 2025, particularly the latter season, was an efficiency-focused operation. The Hoosiers’ offense was so effective last season because Roman Hemby and Kaelon Black, both powerful downhill runners, could be relied on to pick up 4 or so yards on any given run. Do that enough and opposing defensive coordinators have to respond, trying to create tackles for loss and stuffs by committing more resources to the run. That opens up the pass and you get plays like all of those deep shots to Charlie Becker throughout the postseason. There was a shift this past offseason that probably should’ve been immediately apparent when Indiana added Richard, a different kind of back than the program usually leans on. Indiana found success with those powerful efficiency runners like Hemby, Black and Ty Son Lawton, with some burst from Justice Ellison, but Richard was used as an explosive weapon at Boston College. The Hoosiers wanted to get more explosive on the ground. Richard was obviously the focal point and took over immediately as Indiana’s lead back but Beebe Jr. was pretty explosive in his limited attempts in 2025 and had long runs during his time at UAB. Indiana seemed to lean into this, trying to put its personnel in position to do what they do best For a while, that obviously worked. The Hoosiers had one of the most explosive ground games in the sport heading into the Ohio State matchup even after the Nebraska debacle: Most Explosive Offenses 🏈 pic.twitter.com/4FL8IvY4Vv — Cody Nagel (@CodyNagel247) October 11, 2026 Now, not so much. What changed? Well, Indiana’s non-running back personnel and the caliber of opponent it was up against. Indiana lost its starting center and right tackle this past offseason with both Pat Coogan and Kahlil Benson moving onto the NFL. Not only that, tight end Riley Nowakowski departed for the professional ranks as well. That’s multiple key blockers gone. Indiana replaced Coogan by sliding right guard Bray Lynch over to the center spot, making way for Wisconsin transfer Joe Brunner to slide in at the latter’s vacant spot. Adedamola Ajani, who took extensive snaps in the postseason, took over at right tackle. Indiana opted for a few more interesting moves at tight end, adding Brock Schott as a sophomore transfer out of Miami in an already inexperienced room. Indiana added just one experienced piece to fill this select gap in Brunner. The remainder of the moves were either shuffling, rising depth or adding another inexperienced piece. One way or another, these players aren’t performing at the standard set by their predecessors. Lynch, sorry to say, was probably the weaker link on last year’s offensive line. That’s not necessarily awful, the rest of them are either in the NFL or will be soon. It’s also a problem when all of a sudden he’s at the line’s most critical position when it comes to the run. Coogan brought a ton of experience and leadership not only on the offensive line, but to playing center. He’d just helped lead Notre Dame’s offensive line to the National Championship Game. His was going to be a tough act to follow. Indiana is running through the middle of its line, just like last year. Unlike last year, it’s weaker, so it’s finding less success. This wasn’t apparent against the fronts fielded by Northwestern and Rutgers, giving Richard and Beebe Jr. greater room to work with. Against more talented groups at Nebraska and Ohio State? Indiana was physically overmatched and couldn’t get anything going. What could help here? Well, some schematic changes and more of an emphasis on the efficiency of yesteryear could change things, but the personnel isn’t as well built for that either as it was in 2025. The return of Khobie Martin, a back more in that mold, could ail the issue. One way or another, Indiana has to figure out how to run the ball. Soon. Michigan is looming as another tough, big defensive front that’s poised to give the Hoosiers issues.

item.title: NFLPA demands full investigation into Eagles’ care of QB Jalen Hurts
item.description: Two of the NFL’s top health officials backed the Philadelphia Eagles ‘ handling of Jalen Hurts’ blood clots at the league’s fall meeting in New York on Tuesday. By that night, the NFL Players Association had called for a full investigation and raised a problem with the league’s own account of the case. Specialists in London found a clot in Hurts’ left calf on Oct. 10, which the Eagles first described as a “left calf superficial vein thrombosis.” The team’s medical staff and independent doctors concluded he “could safely play” against the Jacksonville Jaguars the next day, and Hurts played the full game in a 19-17 loss. A follow-up ultrasound back in Philadelphia on Oct. 14 showed the clot had moved. On Monday, the Eagles and Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, disclosed a deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning clots had reached both lungs. Hurts is on injured reserve and is expected to miss the rest of the season, though the team said in its joint statement with Lynn that it anticipates “no long-term effects.” Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) drops back to pass during the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images What the NFL said about the Eagles’ doctors “I don’t think you can take that outcome and say there was something flawed about the process,” NFL chief medical officer Allen Sills told reporters . Sills described the Eagles’ medical staff as “incredibly conservative and incredibly vigilant” and rejected the idea that football people had a hand in the decision. “Any idea or any suggestion that a team physician is ever being influenced by a coach, a general manager, a team owner, it just doesn’t happen,” Sills said. Jeff Miller, the NFL executive vice president who oversees player health and safety, called the criticism of the team’s doctors unfounded. “Conservative steps were taken to ensure Jalen Hurts’ health was always made the first priority and continues to be,” Miller said . Miller also said the league has “a complete understanding of the course of events,” built from conversations with the Eagles’ staff, the hospital in London and the doctors involved. The NFL declined to discuss the specifics of Hurts’ case, citing medical privacy, and The Athletic reported the league will not punish the Eagles. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What the NFLPA says the league told the union That understanding came from the same people whose decisions are now being questioned, and the union’s statement, posted to X on Tuesday night, says no review of their work was ever on the table. https://t.co/wZyVLPcXvD — NFLPA (@NFLPA) October 21, 2026 “The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts. In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occur

item.title: The figures that show Mercedes has lost its supremacy in F1 2026
item.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes is confident it can win again in the 2026 Formula 1 season, but is aware it has been facing a bigger challenge than ever from the other top teams. The Silver Arrows triumphed in the opening six grands prix of the campaign, as F1 switched to new technical regulations. Later on, rival upgrades meant Ferrari claimed two victories in Austria and Great Britain, then McLaren ’s Lando Norris took back-to-back wins in Hungary and the Netherlands, and Red Bull’s Max Verstappen prevailed most recently in Malaysia and Singapore. Mercedes didn’t hold off from updating its car either, but the team is well aware its performance advantage has been slashed. That’s despite a healthy lead in both championships, with a maiden world title within reach of Kimi Antonelli in Austin. “I think we've sounded like a bit of a broken record all year, to be honest, because we've been saying how close and competitive this season is, even if we were able to put a good run of wins together earlier in the season,” deputy team principal Bradley Lord commented on the Nu Silver Arrows Radio Show. “That is being borne out. “We saw Ferrari upgrading their car either prior to or up to Baku, Red Bull doing the same. We obviously brought our update to Malaysia and we've seen different levels of hitting the ground running, I guess, with those updates. Last two races, both Red Bull and Ferrari have been more competitive than they had been in the events up to then.” Average gap to pole position Australia to Japan Miami to Belgium Hungary to Singapore Hung. to Sing. (excl. Baku outlier) Mercedes: +0.000s Mercedes: +0.000s Mercedes: +0.162s Ferrari: +0.184s McLaren: +0.567s Ferrari: +0.267s Ferrari: +0.277s Mercedes: +0.189s Ferrari: +0.596s Red Bull: +0.313s McLaren: +0.283s McLaren: +0.191s Red Bull: +0.974s McLaren: +0.432s Red Bull: +0.339s Red Bull: +0.233s “We know we've got a real fight on our hands,” Lord continued, “and it's important that we carry on doing that learning to pull the performance out of the car, so that also we can go into the next races sort of confident that we can fight for wins and continue the sort of two-car points-scoring that we need in order to turn all the hard work so far this year into the result that we're all aiming for, because that was one of the things of the last triple-header – it was quite a messy triple-header in terms of results.” Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes It was a ‘messy triple-header’ indeed, with Antonelli hitting the wall in qualifying in Baku and George Russell suffering a power unit failure in Malaysia, which meant he exceeded his quota in Singapore and started that race from the back of the grid; the Briton went on to crash out of the sprint as he was leading. Read Also: Why Mercedes switched George Russell to its old F1 car spec in Singapore To compound Mercedes’ issues, its latest W17 update has not delivered as much as it was hoping for relative to its rivals – hence very balanced performance among top teams and Red Bull’s return to victory. 2026 marks only the second time four outfits have taken several wins each (Mercedes 11, Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull two) since 1990, after the same outfits shone in 2024. Maybe they miss a little bit, let's say, to be in the top position, but they're very competitive. “And we need to respect McLaren. McLaren, they are the world champion team and they've shown in some races this year that they can be the strongest out there, even with some margin. “There's good possibility that all of these teams will be strong there, and it makes it even more exciting for ourselves. You will try to really squeeze out a bit more from the package, try to optimise our configuration and come back to the top again, like we were in Baku, like we were in Monza, like we've been able to win in Madrid. We can do it again.” Read Also: How can Kimi Antonelli become world champion at F1 US GP? To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Dallas Cowboys: Add Former 2nd-Round Pick to the Squad
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys could add a quarterback after losing Joe Milton III to the Philadelphia Eagles, which leaves them with only two on the roster. One injury to monitor is Dak Prescott , who suffered an apparent rib injury in Week 6 against the Green Bay Packers after taking a shot to the chest. Prescott finished the game, and Brian Schottenheimer told the media he didn’t need X-rays , had the wind knocked out of him, and that the injury was just a bruise. The Dallas Cowboys add a former 2nd-round pick to the squad Sep 29, 2024; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Kyle Trask (2) against the Philadelphia Eagles during the first half at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images According to Todd Archer of ESPN NFL Nation, the Cowboys have signed Kyle Trask to their practice squad, effectively replacing Joe Milton III as the team’s third-string quarterback. Trask can be elevated to the game-day roster three times without penalty; otherwise, a fourth elevation would require a promotion to the active roster. The former Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ second-round pick is on his fourth team and entering his sixth NFL season. The Cowboys are signing QB Kyle Trask to their practice squad, per sources. He replaces Joe Milton III, who signed to the Eagles active roster last week. A second-round pick by Tampa Bay in 2021, he has also been with Atlanta and Carolina. — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) October 20, 2026 The Buccaneers re-signed Kyle Trask to a one-year deal last offseason. Unfortunately, Trask lost the backup quarterback job to Teddy Bridgewater last season, prompting Tampa Bay to release him during roster cuts. He signed with the Falcons’ practice squad in November and spent the last two months there before his contract expired. The Panthers signed Trask in early August, but released him during roster cuts. He remained unsigned through the first six weeks of the regular season. More Cowboys news Nov 23, 2025; Arlington, Texas, USA; A general view of a Dallas Cowboys helmet before the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium. item.title: Anthony Davis says he was called out by a Wizards teammate who's 13 years younger than him
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Anthony Davis is one of the most accomplished players in the NBA, but his young Washington Wizards teammate Tre Johnson still called him out. The 33-year-old veteran is a 10-time All-Star and a former winner of the championship when he was with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020. You would imagine that young players wouldn’t dare question someone like him, but Johnson proved that everyone is equal in a team during a recent practice session. Anthony Davis says Tre Johnson called him out after a poor practice session Johnson is only a second-year pro with the Washington Wizards, but it is clear to see that he is fearless. The 20-year-old, who is 13 years younger than 33-year-old Davis, held the veteran accountable after he missed too many shots in practice. Everybody has a bad day, and when it’s someone who has achieved as much as Davis, you would imagine that his teammates would cut him some slack. However, Johnson mocked his senior teammate and claimed that he looked nothing like a Top 75 player during the practice session. Narrating the incident, Davis told Ben Strober on X : “One day I missed a lot of shots in practice, and Tre Johnson actually came to me, and he was like: ‘Hey, man, you weren’t Top 75 today.’ “You look for that type of stuff, with players who’ll hold you accountable no matter what you’ve done in this league and where you are in this league.” What Johnson did takes a lot of courage. Players of his age wouldn’t have dared to say anything of the sort to an accomplished senior professional in the previous generation. This, however, is a good thing, as every player needs to hold each other accountable if they are to achieve anything meaningful this season.
